topics.embedded: Vehicle computing platforms and latency budgets

papers.title: Latency-aware Road Anomaly Segmentation in Videos: A Photorealistic Dataset and New Metrics
papers.key_idea: Synthetic, photorealism-enhanced video dataset for road anomaly segmentation with two new measures, temporal consistency and latency-aware streaming accuracy, to judge whether an obstacle is flagged early enough to matter.
papers.method: Synthetic driving video made more photorealistic by a GAN conditioned on rendering G-buffers; supervised and unsupervised anomaly-segmentation baselines scored with conventional and the two new metrics.

papers.title: Road Obstacle Video Segmentation
papers.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (book chapter; conference not named in the record read)
papers.key_idea: Argues that road-obstacle segmentation is a temporal task; adapts four benchmarks to video, compares 11 image and video segmentation methods and adds two foundation-model baselines for long sequences.
papers.method: Benchmark curation for video, evaluation of 11 image-based and video-based segmentation methods, two baselines built on vision foundation models.

papers.title: CorrDiff: Adaptive Delay-aware Detector with Temporal Cue Inputs for Real-time Object Detection
papers.key_idea: Streaming-perception detector that uses temporal cues estimated at run time to predict object locations for several future frames and emits the prediction matching real time, compensating communication and computation delay.
papers.method: Delay-aware detector with motion estimation and feature enhancement; scored by mAP for current or next frame and by the streaming metric sAP for future frames, on several GPUs.

papers.title: PAMPOS: Causal Transformer-based Trajectory Prediction for Attack-Agnostic Misbehavior Detection in V2X Networks
papers.venue: ACM Workshop on Wireless Security and Machine Learning
papers.key_idea: Trains a causal transformer decoder on benign vehicle trajectories only and flags V2X messages whose kinematics deviate from its next-step predictions, so no attack-labelled training data is needed.
papers.method: Next-step kinematic prediction; top-K normalized anomaly score that localizes the falsified kinematic feature.

papers.title: Provident vehicle detection at night for advanced driver assistance systems
papers.key_idea: Complete system that detects light artifacts cast by the headlights of oncoming vehicles, localizes and tracks them in 3D, and so announces a vehicle before it is directly visible.
papers.method: Detection of light artifacts in the image, three-dimensional localization and tracking; deployed in a test vehicle to steer a glare-free high beam proactively.

papers.title: Beyond Pixel Uncertainty: Bounding the OoD Objects in Road Scenes
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
papers.key_idea: DetSeg adds object-level reasoning to road anomaly segmentation: detect all objects, suppress in-distribution boxes, keep out-of-distribution proposals, and smooth results across frames with vanishing-point guided matching.
papers.method: Open-world object detection, suppression of in-distribution boxes, optional box-prompted segmentation, vanishing point guided Hungarian matching within a video clip.

papers.title: Debiased Teacher for Day-to-Night Domain Adaptive Object Detection
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
papers.key_idea: Self-training adaptation of a detector from day to night that counters distribution, training and confirmation bias with a physics-prior day-to-night image transform, cross-domain object mixing and calibrated pseudo labels.
papers.method: Teacher-student self-training with three modules: day-to-night domain transforming, cross-domain representation compensating, pseudo-label confirmation calibrating.

papers.title: Learning to See in the Dark
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Introduces a dataset of raw short-exposure low-light images with long-exposure references and a fully convolutional network that maps raw sensor data directly to a usable image.
papers.method: End-to-end trained fully convolutional network on raw sensor data, replacing much of the traditional image processing pipeline.

papers.title: Infrastructure-free NLoS Obstacle Detection for Autonomous Cars
papers.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
papers.key_idea: Detects a hidden moving obstacle from shadows or faint illumination changes on the ground, without fiducial tags, by registering frames with visual odometry before amplifying and classifying the change.
papers.method: Image registration by direct sparse odometry, region of interest on the ground, mean image, colour amplification, dynamic threshold, dynamic-or-static classification; integrated on an autonomous wheelchair and car.

papers.title: World4V2X: A Consistency-driven World Model for Robust V2X Cooperative Perception
papers.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI)
papers.key_idea: World-model framework for V2X cooperative perception that models spatial observability boundaries and temporal consistency beliefs, then refines features by diffusion so detection stays stable under occlusion or degraded observations.
papers.method: Spatial observability modelling, temporal consistency evolution from historical and current frames, consistency-guided diffusion-based reconstruction.

papers.title: Misbehavior detection with spatio-temporal graph neural networks
papers.key_idea: Gives an algorithm that converts classical V2X misbehaviour datasets into graph form and proposes a spatio-temporal graph neural network that detects misbehaving activity.
papers.method: Dataset conversion to graphs plus a graph neural network detector; details not read.

papers.title: VeReMi NextGen: A Dataset for Evaluating Misbehavior Detection Systems in VANETs
papers.key_idea: Simulated V2X message dataset for misbehaviour detection with urban and highway scenarios, three driver profiles, 15 attack types, fixed training, validation and test sets, and a public generator.
papers.method: Generated with the InTAS traffic scenario and Eclipse MOSAIC; attacks integrated in post-processing; difficulty checked with an existing misbehaviour detection system.

papers.title: V2X-Real: a Large-Scale Dataset for Vehicle-to-Everything Cooperative Perception
papers.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (book chapter; conference not named in the record read)
papers.key_idea: Real-world cooperative-perception dataset recorded with two connected automated vehicles and two smart infrastructure units carrying LiDAR and multi-view cameras, with benchmarks for four cooperation modes.
papers.method: Data collection and annotation; multi-class multi-agent benchmarks of existing cooperative perception methods.

papers.title: V2X-Sim: Multi-Agent Collaborative Perception Dataset and Benchmark for Autonomous Driving
papers.key_idea: Simulated multi-agent perception dataset with roadside-unit and multi-vehicle sensor recordings, several sensor modalities and ground truths, plus an open testbed and benchmark for collaborative detection, tracking and segmentation.
papers.method: Simulation-based data generation; benchmark of collaborative perception algorithms on three tasks.

papers.title: BDD100K: A Diverse Driving Dataset for Heterogeneous Multitask Learning
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Driving video dataset of 100K videos annotated for 10 tasks, with geographic, environmental and weather diversity, and a benchmark for heterogeneous multitask learning.
papers.method: Dataset construction and a multitask benchmark across the 10 tasks.

papers.title: ACDC: The Adverse Conditions Dataset with Correspondences for Semantic Driving Scene Understanding
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
papers.key_idea: Driving images under fog, night, rain and snow with pixel-level annotation, a matching normal-condition image of the same scene and a mask separating clear from uncertain image regions.
papers.method: Dataset with correspondences; study of supervised and unsupervised methods on the adverse domains.

papers.title: A Dataset for Provident Vehicle Detection at Night
papers.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
papers.key_idea: Night-time rural driving images with annotated oncoming vehicles, their light sources and the reflections they cause, so that vehicles can be detected from reflections before they are directly visible.
papers.method: Keypoint annotation of light instances; metrics for several task formulations; baseline results with standard and custom object detectors.

papers.title: Lost and Found: Detecting Small Road Hazards for Self-Driving Vehicles
papers.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
papers.key_idea: Stereo-vision method that tests free-space against obstacle hypotheses on local patches in disparity space, evaluated on a new lost-cargo sequence dataset with pixel-level labels.
papers.method: Statistical hypothesis tests in disparity space on independent local patches, without a global road model; comparison with stereo baselines.

papers.title: CODA: A Real-World Road Corner Case Dataset for Object Detection in Autonomous Driving
papers.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (book chapter; conference not named in the record read)
papers.key_idea: Real driving scenes selected for object-level corner cases outside the usual categories, built to test object detectors on rare and novel objects.
papers.method: Dataset curation; evaluation of standard detectors and of an open-world detector.

papers.title: M2P2: A Multi-Modal Passive Perception Dataset for Off-Road Mobility in Extreme Low-Light Conditions
papers.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
papers.key_idea: Off-road dataset recorded with thermal, event and stereo RGB cameras plus LiDAR ground truth, meant to enable mobility by passive sensing in low-light and no-light conditions.
papers.method: Multi-modal sensor suite with a multi-sensor calibration procedure; demonstrations with end-to-end learning and classical planning.

papers.title: YOLOX: Exceeding YOLO Series in 2021
papers.key_idea: Anchor-free YOLO variant with a decoupled head and SimOTA label assignment, released across model sizes down to a Nano model with 0.91M parameters.
papers.method: Anchor-free detection, decoupled head, SimOTA label assignment; deploy versions for ONNX, TensorRT, NCNN and OpenVINO.

papers.title: Real-time Object Detection for Streaming Perception
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Streaming-perception detector that learns to predict objects in the next frame with a dual-flow module and a trend-aware loss, so that latency and accuracy are judged by one metric.
papers.method: DualFlow Perception module (dynamic and static flows) and a Trend-Aware Loss with a trend factor for objects of different speeds.

papers.title: Slicing Aided Hyper Inference and Fine-tuning for Small Object Detection
papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP)
papers.key_idea: Open-source framework that slices an image into tiles for inference and fine-tuning, raising small-object detection accuracy on top of any detector without retraining it.
papers.method: Slicing aided inference and slicing aided fine-tuning; integrated with Detectron2, MMDetection and YOLOv5 models.

papers.title: Scikit-learn: Machine Learning in Python
papers.key_idea: Python module that packages a wide range of supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms behind a consistent interface for medium-scale problems.
papers.method: Software library; emphasis on ease of use, performance, documentation and API consistency.

papers.title: Searching for MobileNetV3
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
papers.key_idea: MobileNetV3 networks found by hardware-aware architecture search with NetAdapt and design refinements, released as Large and Small models for high and low resource use.
papers.method: Hardware-aware network architecture search, NetAdapt, new architecture elements; a light segmentation decoder (LR-ASPP).

papers.title: Depth Anything V2
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37
papers.key_idea: Monocular depth model trained with synthetic labelled images, a larger teacher and pseudo-labelled real images, released in sizes from about 25M to 1.3B parameters.
papers.method: Synthetic labelled images for the teacher, large-scale pseudo-labelled real images for the student models; metric-depth fine-tuning; a new evaluation benchmark.

papers.title: PyTorch: An Imperative Style, High-Performance Deep Learning Library
papers.key_idea: Describes the design principles and architecture of PyTorch, a deep learning library with an imperative Python style that stays efficient and supports hardware accelerators.
papers.method: Software library paper; runtime design and benchmarks of subsystems.

papers.title: Alpamayo-R1: Bridging Reasoning and Action Prediction for Generalizable Autonomous Driving in the Long Tail
papers.key_idea: Vision-language-action driving model that couples chain-of-causation reasoning with a diffusion-based trajectory decoder, trained by supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
papers.method: Cosmos-Reason vision-language backbone plus a diffusion-based trajectory decoder; multi-stage training.

papers.title: The Architectural Implications of Autonomous Driving
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Twenty-Third International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems (ASPLOS 2018)
papers.key_idea: Derives timing constraints for a full driving pipeline: process each frame within 100 ms at a rate of at least once per 100 ms, judged by tail latency; compares CPU, GPU, FPGA and ASIC acceleration.
papers.method: End-to-end pipeline (object detection, tracking, localization, planning) profiled on KITTI on an Intel server; detection, tracking and localization accelerated on GPU, FPGA and ASIC; mean, 99th and 99.99th percentile latency and power measured.

papers.title: Computing Systems for Autonomous Driving: State of the Art and Challenges
papers.key_idea: Survey of computing systems for autonomous driving, framed by seven performance metrics, nine key technologies and twelve challenges; argues current systems still fail to understand complex real traffic in real time.
papers.method: Literature survey; the abstract names sensors, computer vision, machine learning, hardware acceleration and vehicle communication (DSRC, C-V2X, 5G) as the enabling technologies.

papers.title: Compute Solution for Tesla's Full Self-Driving Computer
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: the compute design of a production vehicle's full self-driving computer. A 2024 review (lead 1, not a row) describes two custom SoCs, each with CPUs, a GPU and two neural network accelerators.
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only).

papers.title: Autoware on Board: Enabling Autonomous Vehicles with Embedded Systems
papers.venue: 2018 ACM/IEEE 9th International Conference on Cyber-Physical Systems (ICCPS)
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: running the Autoware open-source autonomous-driving software on embedded systems to enable autonomous vehicles.
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only).

papers.title: Edge Computing for Autonomous Driving: Opportunities and Challenges
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: review of edge computing for autonomous driving, with its opportunities and its challenges.
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only).

papers.title: Efficient Computing Platform Design for Autonomous Driving Systems
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 26th Asia and South Pacific Design Automation Conference (ASP-DAC 2021)
papers.key_idea: Argues that a practical driving computer needs dedicated optimisation and proposes, among other levels, custom hardware accelerators for the pre- and post-processing around deep learning inference.
papers.method: Platform design across levels; at the hardware level, customised accelerators for pre- and post-processing of deep learning (abstract snippet).

papers.title: Run Your 3D Object Detector on NVIDIA Jetson Platforms:A Benchmark Analysis
papers.key_idea: Benchmarks deep-learning 3D object detectors on every commercially available Jetson board (Nano, TX2, NX, AGX) and measures what TensorRT optimisation changes in speed and resource use.
papers.method: State-of-the-art 3D detectors (point-cloud processing) run on four Jetson boards with and without TensorRT; accuracy, frames per second and resource utilisation compared.

papers.title: Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only Inference
papers.venue: 2018 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: a quantization scheme with a matching training procedure so that a network runs inference in integer arithmetic only, for efficient deployment.
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only).

papers.title: A Deep Learning Framework Performance Evaluation to Use YOLO in Nvidia Jetson Platform
papers.key_idea: Compares TensorFlow, TensorFlow-TensorRT, TensorRT and TensorFlow Lite for YOLOv4 on a Jetson AGX Xavier, measuring CPU and GPU use, accuracy, latency and power with the Jetson monitoring tool.
papers.method: Inference measurement that fuses the Jetson monitoring tool with TensorFlow and TensorRT code; YOLOv4 evaluated per framework.

papers.title: Deployment of Deep Neural Networks for Object Detection on Edge AI Devices with Runtime Optimization
papers.venue: 2021 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)
papers.key_idea: Deploys object-detection networks on edge AI devices and compares runtime optimisation tools; a full-text snippet reports lower inference time with both tools, TensorRT fastest, and a further cut with TensorRT INT8.
papers.method: Not read beyond one passage; TensorRT is the only tool named in the passage seen.

papers.title: Benchmarking YOLOv8 Variants for Object Detection Efficiency on Jetson Orin NX for Edge Computing Applications
papers.key_idea: Benchmarks YOLOv8 variants on a Jetson Orin NX across input and batch sizes, comparing PyTorch with TensorRT on latency, throughput and memory, with vehicle and package detection use cases.
papers.method: YOLOv8 variants under PyTorch and TensorRT on a Jetson Orin NX (search snippet: JetPack with CUDA 11.4 and TensorRT 8.5, FP16); latency, frame throughput and memory per batch size.

papers.title: MLPerf Inference Benchmark
papers.venue: 2020 ACM/IEEE 47th Annual International Symposium on Computer Architecture (ISCA)
papers.key_idea: Industry inference benchmark defining four load scenarios; single-stream scores the 90th-percentile latency, multistream models multi-camera driver assistance under a latency bound, with query counts fixed for statistically confident tail latency.
papers.method: A load generator issues queries per scenario (single-stream, multistream, server, offline); minimum query counts follow from tail percentile, confidence and margin; minimum run time of 60 s so power management and DVFS reach equilibrium (arXiv HTML passages).

papers.title: Pylot: A Modular Platform for Exploring Latency-Accuracy Tradeoffs in Autonomous Vehicles
papers.venue: 2021 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: a modular autonomous-vehicle platform built to explore trade-offs between latency and accuracy of the driving pipeline's components.
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only).

papers.title: Concurrent Video-Stream Workload and Sustained Thermal Conditions Affect the Latency and Real-Time Performance of Object Detection on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano
papers.key_idea: Measures how one to three concurrent camera streams and sustained heat change inference and pipeline latency of a YOLO detector on a Jetson Orin Nano against a 100 ms real-time reference.
papers.method: The same dashcam video fed as one, two or three simultaneous streams; GPU use and temperature logged under low and high temperature; three 60 s trials per condition; mean, p99 and share of frames over 100 ms.

papers.title: End-to-End Latency Optimization for Containerized ROS 2 Autonomous Driving Software
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: end-to-end latency of autonomous-driving software built on ROS 2 and run in containers, and how to reduce it.
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only).

papers.title: Priority Optimization for Autonomous Driving Systems to Meet End-to-End Latency Constraints
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: assigning priorities among the tasks of a driving system so that its end-to-end latency constraints are met.
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only).

papers.title: TensorRT-Based Framework and Optimization Methodology for Deep Learning Inference on Jetson Boards
papers.venue: ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems
papers.key_idea: TensorRT framework that splits a network's layers between the GPU and the neural processing unit of a Jetson AGX Xavier, with threading, pipelining, buffer assignment and network duplication tuned by a heuristic.
papers.method: Layer-to-processor allocation between GPU and NPU plus multi-threading, pipelining, buffer assignment and network duplication; a heuristic balances pipeline stages, then parameters are fine-tuned; nine real-life benchmarks.

papers.title: An Analysis of ISO 26262: Machine Learning and Safety in Automotive Software
papers.key_idea: Analyses how machine learning inside automotive software affects the ISO 26262 safety lifecycle and recommends how the standard could be adapted to accommodate ML components.
papers.method: Analysis of the ISO 26262 lifecycle against the properties of ML; recommendations for adapting the standard.

papers.title: Workflow between ISO 26262 and ISO 21448 Standards for Autonomous Vehicles
papers.key_idea: Proposes a detailed workflow aligning ISO 26262 functional-safety activities with iterative ISO 21448 (SOTIF) activities, with guidance on when a SOTIF-driven design change affects the functional-safety analysis and vice versa.
papers.method: Activity mapping between the two standards; change-impact guidelines; agile development considerations.

papers.title: Challenges in Autonomous Vehicle Testing and Validation
papers.venue: SAE International Journal of Transportation Safety
papers.key_idea: Identifies five challenge areas for testing autonomous vehicles under the ISO 26262 V model, including inductive learning, and recommends a monitor/actuator pair separating complex autonomy functions from simpler safety functions.
papers.method: Position paper mapping test challenges to the V model; solution approaches: phased deployment with relaxed operational scenarios, monitor/actuator architecture, fault injection.

papers.title: Complying with ISO 26262 and ISO/SAE 21434: A Safety and Security Co-Analysis Method for Intelligent Connected Vehicle
papers.key_idea: Merges system-theoretic process analysis with the concept phases of ISO 26262 and ISO/SAE 21434 to derive safety and security requirements together, demonstrated on an autonomous emergency braking system.
papers.method: STPA-SafeSec with interface elements added to the physical component diagram; loss scenario tree for unsafe or unsecure control actions; unified risk assessment; case study.

papers.title: DNNGuard: An Elastic Heterogeneous DNN Accelerator Architecture against Adversarial Attacks
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Twenty-Fifth International Conference on Architectural Support for Programming Languages and Operating Systems (ASPLOS 2020)
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: an elastic heterogeneous accelerator architecture that defends DNNs against adversarial attacks; its journal successor (P2-P2523) runs the target network and a detection network side by side.
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only).

papers.title: A Hybrid Sparse-dense Defensive DNN Accelerator Architecture against Adversarial Example Attacks
papers.venue: ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems
papers.key_idea: sDNNGuard: an elastic heterogeneous accelerator that executes the target DNN and an adversarial-example detection algorithm or network simultaneously, supporting dense and sparse workloads with elastic on-chip resource scheduling.
papers.method: Heterogeneous accelerator with a CPU core for non-DNN layers, elastic on-chip buffer and compute management, and an extended AI instruction set for synchronisation and task scheduling.

papers.title: CyberDet: Real-time Adversarial Attacks Detection for Autonomous Robots and Self-driving Cars
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: a detector of adversarial attacks for autonomous robots and self-driving cars that the title describes as real-time.
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only).

papers.title: Detection Latency as a Constraint on the Architectural Complexity of Real-Time AI-based Adversarial Detectors
papers.key_idea: Treats detection latency as a design constraint for adversarial detectors and maps accuracy against latency for statistical, ensemble and transformer detectors on CPU, GPU and edge TPU.
papers.method: Latency-aware evaluation over detector architectures (layer count, kernel size, attention heads, feature dimension) against FGSM, PGD and C&W examples on CPU, GPU and edge TPU.

papers.title: Optimizing Driver Monitoring System Performance on TI-TDA4VM Edge Device
papers.venue: 2024 International Mobile, Intelligent, and Ubiquitous Computing Conference (MIUCC)
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: optimisation of a driver monitoring system's performance on the TI TDA4VM edge device (system on chip).
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only).

papers.title: Benchmarking the NXP i.MX8M+ neural processing unit: smart parking case study
papers.key_idea: Benchmarks the NPU of an NXP i.MX8M Plus with a two-stage GStreamer pipeline (licence-plate detection, then character inference), measuring execution time and CPU use in serial and parallel runs.
papers.method: GStreamer inference pipeline; licence-plate detection offloaded to the NPU; execution-time and CPU-usage sampling.

papers.title: Robust Physical-World Attacks on Deep Learning Visual Classification
papers.key_idea: RP2 crafts perturbations, realised as black and white stickers, that survive changing physical conditions and viewpoints and make road sign classifiers output a chosen wrong class on a real stop sign.
papers.method: Robust Physical Perturbations (RP2) optimisation plus a two-stage lab and field evaluation protocol

papers.title: Physical Adversarial Examples for Object Detectors
papers.key_idea: Extends sticker and poster attacks from classifiers to detectors: a Disappearance Attack makes a stop sign vanish for YOLOv2, and a preliminary Creation Attack makes stickers trigger detections of nonexistent objects.
papers.method: Poster and sticker perturbations optimised against YOLOv2; transfer tested on Faster R-CNN; lab and outdoor video

papers.title: Adversarial Patch
papers.key_idea: Optimises a single printable patch that, placed anywhere in a scene, makes an image classifier output a chosen target class; universal across scenes and robust to transformations.
papers.method: Patch optimised over random placements and transformations against image classifiers

papers.title: Naturalistic Physical Adversarial Patch for Object Detectors
papers.key_idea: Samples the learned image manifold of a pretrained GAN (BigGAN, StyleGAN) to produce natural-looking adversarial patches that attack object detectors in the physical world.
papers.method: Optimisation over the latent space of a pretrained GAN to choose the patch image

papers.title: Patch of Invisibility: Naturalistic Physical Black-Box Adversarial Attacks on Object Detectors
papers.venue: ECML-PKDD 2024 Workshop on Machine Learning for Cybersecurity
papers.key_idea: Black-box, gradient-free attack that samples a pretrained GAN's image manifold to create naturalistic patches for object detectors, needing only model outputs, with reported state-of-the-art results among black-box attacks.
papers.method: BBNP: gradient-free search over a GAN latent space using only detector outputs

papers.title: FCA: Learning a 3D Full-Coverage Vehicle Camouflage for Multi-View Physical Adversarial Attack
papers.key_idea: Paints an optimised camouflage texture over the whole 3D vehicle surface so the vehicle evades detectors across views, distances and partial occlusion, unlike single planar patches.
papers.method: Renders camouflage on a 3D vehicle, transfers it into photorealistic scenes with a transformation function, optimises the texture with a dedicated loss

papers.title: ACTIVE: Towards Highly Transferable 3D Physical Camouflage for Universal and Robust Vehicle Evasion
papers.key_idea: Universal 3D camouflage for vehicles: one texture, a stealth loss and smoothness terms, tested on 15 detector models, with transfer to other vehicle classes, segmentation models and the real world.
papers.method: Common-texture rendering plus stealth, smooth and camouflage losses optimised against detectors

papers.title: ShapeShifter: Robust Physical Adversarial Attack on Faster R-CNN Object Detector
papers.key_idea: Adapts Expectation over Transformation to object detection so printed adversarial stop signs stay mis-detected by Faster R-CNN across viewing distances, angles and lighting.
papers.method: Expectation over Transformation applied to the multi-box detector loss; printed stop sign perturbations

papers.title: PatchZero: Defending against Adversarial Patch Attacks by Detecting and Zeroing the Patch
papers.key_idea: Pixel-level patch detector that zeros out the detected patch region with mean pixel values before the unchanged classifier or detector runs; relies on patches being highly textured and unlike natural images.
papers.method: Pixel-level patch detection, mean-value repainting, two-stage adversarial training against adaptive attacks

papers.title: Segment and Complete: Defending Object Detectors against Adversarial Patch Attacks with Robust Patch Detection
papers.key_idea: Trains a patch segmenter for pixel-level localisation, hardens it by self adversarial training, then removes the whole patch with a shape-completion step that carries a Hamming-distance guarantee; no detector retraining needed.
papers.method: Patch segmenter plus robust shape completion; evaluated on physical patch photos

papers.title: DetectorGuard: Provably Securing Object Detectors against Localized Patch Hiding Attacks
papers.key_idea: A robust classifier predicts objectness at every location and each objectness must be explained by the boxes of a conventional detector; unexplained objectness raises an attack alert, otherwise detector output is used.
papers.method: Objectness explaining: robust-classifier objectness map checked against detector boxes, alert on mismatch, provable robustness for certified objects

papers.title: ObjectSeeker: Certifiably Robust Object Detection against Patch Hiding Attacks via Patch-agnostic Masking
papers.key_idea: Patch-agnostic masking removes any possible patch region without knowing its shape, size or location so a vanilla detector can run on masked images; a certification step shows which objects are provably still detected.
papers.method: Masked-image inference with box pruning plus a certification procedure

papers.title: PatchCleanser: Certifiably Robust Defense against Adversarial Patches for Any Image Classifier
papers.key_idea: Two rounds of pixel masking neutralise a patch: unanimous predictions on one-masked images pass, disagreements are settled by a second round; works with any image classifier and gives certified robustness.
papers.method: Double masking with prediction-disagreement logic and certification

papers.title: NAPGuard: Towards Detecting Naturalistic Adversarial Patches
papers.key_idea: Detects naturalistic adversarial patches by directionally modulating aggressive and natural features during training and inference, because earlier detectors blur these two natures and generalise poorly to natural-looking patches.
papers.method: Critical feature modulation framework for patch detection

papers.title: Jedi: Entropy-Based Localization and Removal of Adversarial Patches
papers.key_idea: Finds patch regions by local entropy, which stays high even for naturalistic patches, completes them with an autoencoder and repairs the image; model-agnostic, with no change to the protected model.
papers.method: Entropy analysis for candidate regions, autoencoder completion, inpainting-style repair

papers.title: PAD: Patch-Agnostic Defense against Adversarial Patch Attacks
papers.key_idea: Exploits two inherent properties of adversarial patches, semantic independence and spatial heterogeneity, to localise and remove them with no prior attack knowledge or extra training, compatible with any pre-trained detector.
papers.method: Patch localisation from semantic-independence and image-quality cues, then removal

papers.title: The Outline of Deception: Physical Adversarial Attacks on Traffic Signs Using Edge Patches
papers.key_idea: TESP-Attack puts adversarial patches along the sign edge, using instance-segmentation masks that follow the sign shape and colour, texture and frequency constraints, to blend with the background while fooling sign classifiers.
papers.method: Edge-aligned masks from instance segmentation, U-Net patch generator, colour, texture and frequency-domain constraints, limited query budget

papers.title: Dynamic Adversarial Attacks on Autonomous Driving Systems
papers.key_idea: Dynamic patches shown on a screen mounted on another moving vehicle fool a vehicle's object detector without being attached to the target, using a screen-transformation network and a positional loss.
papers.method: Screen Image Transformation Network simulating environmental effects; positional loss in adversarial training

papers.title: Revisiting Physical-World Adversarial Attack on Traffic Sign Recognition: A Commercial Systems Perspective
papers.key_idea: Measures physical-world attacks against commercial traffic sign recognition systems; some attacks reach 100% success on one functionality but not in general, and a spatial memorisation design lowers system-level success.
papers.method: Large-scale measurement on commercial systems plus new attack-success metrics that model the memorisation design

papers.title: The Translucent Patch: A Physical and Universal Attack on Object Detectors
papers.key_idea: A translucent patch placed on the camera lens, not on the object, hides all instances of a chosen class from detectors while the optimisation tries to keep other classes detectable.
papers.method: Optimisation of a universal translucent pattern with a loss that hides the target class and spares the others

papers.title: Advertising or adversarial? AdvSign: Artistic advertising sign camouflage for target physical attacking to object detector
papers.key_idea: Turns adversarial patterns into artistic advertising signs attachable to carriers such as carry-bags and vehicle stickers, aiming at physical attacks on object detectors that pass as ordinary advertising.
papers.method: Adversarial patterns designed as artistic advertising signs

papers.title: Adversarial Attacks on Traffic Sign Recognition: A Survey
papers.key_idea: Surveys digital and real-world attacks on traffic sign detection and classification models and points to research areas that need more work.
papers.method: Literature survey

papers.title: Low-Cost FPGA-Based Hybrid Defence Against Sticker Attacks for Traffic-Sign Classification

papers.title: Explainable and Trustworthy Traffic Sign Detection for Safe Autonomous Driving: An Inductive Logic Programming Approach
papers.key_idea: Rule-based (Inductive Logic Programming) stop sign detection from high-level features such as shape, colour and text, robust to RP2 and AdvCam attacks and fully explainable, with little training data.

papers.title: We Can Always Catch You: Detecting Adversarial Patched Objects WITH or WITHOUT Signature

papers.title: Exploiting Multi-Object Relationships for Detecting Adversarial Attacks in Complex Scenes

papers.title: Multi-Task Consistency-based Detection of Adversarial Attacks

papers.key_idea: Adversarial Spectrum Defense analyses adversarial patterns across frequency scales with a discrete wavelet transform and combines this with adversarial training, aiming at patch-based and texture-based physical attacks under adaptive attackers.

papers.title: Signals Are All You Need: Detecting and Mitigating Digital and Real-World Adversarial Patches Using Signal-Based Features

papers.title: Detection of Physical Adversarial Attacks on Traffic Signs for Autonomous Vehicles

papers.title: Detecting and Removing Adversarial Patches using Frequency Signatures
papers.key_idea: Corner Cutter finds the frequency-domain signature that patch construction leaves, isolates high-frequency signals and removes the matching pixels; claimed robust to unseen patches and adaptive attacks (abstract of an earlier submission).

papers.title: I Don't Know You, But I Can Catch You: Real-Time Defense against Diverse Adversarial Patches for Object Detectors
papers.key_idea: NutNet uses an autoencoder trained on small image blocks and flags blocks with large reconstruction error as patches, aiming at real-time defense against both hiding and appearing attacks of diverse patches.
papers.method: Block-wise autoencoder reconstruction error to locate and mask patches

papers.title: X-Detect: explainable adversarial patch detection for object detectors in retail
papers.key_idea: Ensemble of explainable-by-design detectors (object extraction, scene manipulation, feature transformation) that flags adversarial patches in real time, explains each alert and handles unfamiliar attacks; evaluated in a retail smart-shopping-cart setting.
papers.method: Two base detectors, an object extraction detector and a scene processing detector, decide whether to raise an alert

papers.title: SentiNet: Detecting Localized Universal Attacks Against Deep Learning Systems
papers.key_idea: Detects localized universal attacks, including adversarial patches, without training a model or knowing the attack, by combining model interpretability (saliency) with object-detection techniques; reported robust to adaptive adversaries.
papers.method: Model-interpretability (Grad-CAM saliency) and object-detection techniques used as detection mechanisms; no model training

papers.title: A Real-Time Defense Against Object Vanishing Adversarial Patch Attacks for Object Detection in Autonomous Vehicles
papers.venue: Lecture Notes of the ICST (Springer chapter, practitioner paper)
papers.key_idea: ADAV checks if detector output is temporally consistent with a previous reference frame to detect object-vanishing patches, then localises adversarial pixels with gradient-based attribution; both stages target low latency.

papers.title: Fast and Lightweight Vision-Language Model for Adversarial Traffic Sign Detection
papers.key_idea: Vision-language adversarial sign detection (ViLAS) works alongside the traffic sign recognition model to flag adversarial attacks on road sign recognition; the title claims a fast, lightweight vision-language model.

papers.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Explainable AI for Adversarial Attack Detection in Traffic Sign Recognition Systems
papers.key_idea: Tests explanation-space detection: NoiseCAM attention maps expose inconsistencies in model attention to flag adversarial traffic sign images, assessed as a binary detector against a Gaussian-noise baseline on GTSRB.

papers.title: Detection of Adversarial Physical Attacks in Time-Series Image Data
papers.key_idea: VisionGuard* couples a real-time single-image detector of physical attacks (VisionGuard) with majority voting over frames, and studies theoretically and experimentally how voting improves adversarial detectors in video.

papers.title: AEGIS: A Semantic GAN and Evidential Learning Framework for Robust Adversarial Detection in Vision Sensors
papers.key_idea: Two-stage adversarial detector for image classification: a semantic GAN discriminator filters visually inconsistent inputs, then test-time instability features feed an evidential (Dirichlet) classifier that outputs calibrated uncertainty.

papers.title: REAP: A Large-Scale Realistic Adversarial Patch Benchmark
papers.key_idea: Digital benchmark of over 14,000 real traffic signs from Mapillary Vistas, each with geometric and lighting transforms so a digitally generated patch can be rendered realistically, to evaluate patch attacks under real-world conditions.

papers.title: APRICOT: A Dataset of Physical Adversarial Attacks on Object Detection
papers.key_idea: Over 1,000 annotated photographs of printed adversarial patches in public places, with natural variation in position, distance, lighting and viewing angle, aimed at three COCO-trained detectors; also gives defense baselines.
papers.method: Photographed printed patches with annotations; defense baselines include a detector supervised on synthetic data and unsupervised kernel density estimation, Bayesian uncertainty and reconstruction error

papers.title: Revisiting Adversarial Patch Defenses on Object Detectors: Unified Evaluation, Large-Scale Dataset, and New Insights
papers.key_idea: Unified benchmark of 11 patch defenses, 13 attacks and 11 detectors with 4 metrics, plus a 94,000-image patch dataset; finds naturalistic patches hard because of data distribution, not high frequency.
papers.method: Benchmark of 11 representative defenses against 13 patch attacks on 11 detectors, adaptive attacks, analysis of metrics

papers.title: Effects of Real-Life Traffic Sign Alteration on YOLOv7- an Object Recognition Model
papers.key_idea: Measures how benign real-life traffic sign alterations (shape, colour, content, visibility, angle, background) degrade YOLOv7 detection and classification, using a public dataset and no adversarial algorithms.

papers.title: AdvScene: Rethinking Adversarial Patch Evaluation Through Scene Robustness
papers.key_idea: Measures the scene robustness of adversarial patches in reconstructed real environments as a function of viewpoint, distance and scene context, through a patch-to-scene embedding (APSE) that keeps attack-critical appearance across views.
papers.method: Scene-grounded evaluation framework with Adversarial Patch-to-Scene Embedding (APSE) under cross-view consistency constraints

papers.title: PatchBlock: A Lightweight Defense Against Adversarial Patches for Embedded EdgeAI Devices
papers.key_idea: PatchBlock is a lightweight framework to detect and neutralize adversarial patches in images on embedded EdgeAI devices; test platforms listed in the paper text include a Jetson Orin Nano and a laptop.

papers.title: Real-time detectors for digital and physical adversarial inputs to perception systems

papers.key_idea: Title-level: a single-stage GAN-based defense for traffic sign classification under adversarial patch attacks; method, data and results not read.

papers.key_idea: Passive physical attack: occluders redirect sunlight into bright lane-like 'negative shadows' that lane detectors mistake for lane markings; a lightweight brightness-normalising pre-filter is proposed as a defense.

papers.title: AdvShadow: camouflaged adversarial attacks via conditional diffusion model-generated shadows
papers.key_idea: Title only: camouflaged adversarial attack whose perturbation is a shadow produced by a conditional diffusion model. Abstract not read; target models, digital or physical setting and results UNVERIFIED.

papers.title: Light can be Dangerous: Stealthy and Effective Physical-world Adversarial Attack by Spot Light
papers.key_idea: Title only: physical-world attack that uses a spot of light as the perturbation; the title echoes the CVPR 2022 shadow paper. Abstract not read; method and results UNVERIFIED.

papers.title: Fight light with light: A review of physical adversarial attack within light transmission pipeline
papers.key_idea: Title only: review of physical adversarial attacks organised along the light transmission pipeline. Abstract not read; whether shadow attacks are covered, and how, is UNVERIFIED.

papers.title: Shadows Aren't So Dangerous After All: A Fast and Robust Defense Against Shadow-Based Adversarial Attacks
papers.key_idea: Input-side defense for road-sign classifiers: add binary adaptive-threshold and edge maps to the image so natural-looking shadow perturbations lose effect, with little loss of benign accuracy.
papers.method: Augments source images with adaptive-threshold and edge maps; recasts shadow attacks as epsilon-bounded perturbation attacks.

papers.title: Distilling Vision-Language Models for Robust Traffic Sign Perception in Autonomous Vehicles
papers.key_idea: Training-only framework (LAMDA) that aligns sign features with frozen text-prototype banks from a vision-language model; extra modules are dropped at inference, so run-time cost does not grow.
papers.method: Two auxiliary losses on fixed prototype banks built from sign descriptions with a frozen OpenCLIP text encoder; no adversarial examples used in training.

papers.title: Time Traveling to Defend Against Adversarial Example Attacks in Image Classification
papers.key_idea: Defense that classifies past street-view images of the same sign and takes a majority vote, so a recent physical change such as a sticker, light or shadow is outvoted.

papers.title: Sequence-Preserving Dual-FoV Defense for Traffic Sign and Light Recognition in Autonomous Vehicles
papers.key_idea: Three-layer defense stack for sign and traffic-light recognition: feature squeezing, defensive distillation and entropy-based anomaly detection, plus temporal voting over time-aligned image sequences from two fields of view.
papers.method: Unified defense stack evaluated on aligned RGB sequences in four operating domains: highway, night, rain, urban.

papers.title: Traffic Sign Recognition Under Visual Perturbations: Shadows, Light Patches, and Simulated Obstructions
papers.venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
papers.key_idea: Title only: traffic sign recognition tested under shadows, light patches and simulated obstructions. Abstract not read; whether the perturbations are adversarial, which models were tested and any defense are UNVERIFIED.

papers.title: Video Shadow Detection via Spatio-Temporal Interpolation Consistency Training
papers.venue: 2022 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Trains an image shadow detector with unlabeled video frames using spatial and temporal interpolation-consistency constraints, so predictions stay temporally consistent without video labels.
papers.method: Spatio-temporal interpolation consistency training with a scale-aware network and a scale-consistency constraint.

papers.title: Learning Shadow Correspondence for Video Shadow Detection
papers.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (book chapter; conference name not shown in the Crossref record)
papers.key_idea: Plug-in module that pulls together features of the same shadow region across neighbouring frames, so video shadow masks stay stable when illumination and background texture change.
papers.method: Weakly supervised pixel-wise shadow correspondence across frames; adds a temporal-stability metric.

papers.title: SCOTCH and SODA: A Transformer Video Shadow Detection Framework
papers.venue: 2023 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Video shadow detector with a deformation-aware attention module (SODA) and a contrastive learning scheme (SCOTCH) to cope with large shadow shape changes between frames.
papers.method: Video self-attention along shadow deformation trajectories plus contrastive learning across videos.

papers.title: Detect Any Shadow: Segment Anything for Video Shadow Detection
papers.key_idea: Fine-tunes the Segment Anything model to detect shadows and propagates a first-frame mask through the video with a long short-term attention network, with faster inference than earlier video shadow detectors.
papers.method: SAM fine-tuned on ViSha with box prompts; long short-term attention propagates the mask across frames.

papers.title: Temporal Feature Warping for Video Shadow Detection
papers.key_idea: Aligns features of neighbouring frames with optical-flow warping across several network layers, to detect moving and small shadows in video better than co-attention.
papers.method: Optical-flow-based warping module applied at multiple layers to combine local and semantic information from adjacent frames.

papers.title: DTTNet: Improving Video Shadow Detection via Dark-Aware Guidance and Tokenized Temporal Modeling
papers.key_idea: Video shadow detector that separates shadows from dark objects with text-guided features and summarizes cross-frame shadow cues into temporal tokens for sequence encoding with little extra computation.
papers.method: Vision-language match module and dark-aware semantic block, plus a tokenized temporal block that decouples spatial and temporal learning.

papers.title: Video Instance Shadow Detection Under the Sun and Sky
papers.key_idea: Semi-supervised video instance shadow detection that tracks shadow-object pairs across frames, handling occlusion and temporary disappearance; introduces the SOBA-VID videos and the SOAP-VID metric.
papers.method: Two-stage training: contrastive cross-frame pairing on labeled images, then cycle-consistency tracking on unlabeled videos with a retrieval mechanism.

papers.title: FastInstShadow: A Simple Query-Based Model for Instance Shadow Detection
papers.key_idea: Query-based transformer that detects shadow-object pairs together, claiming real-time processing at moderate resolution and higher accuracy than the previous best method on SOBA.
papers.method: Association transformer decoder with two dual-path decoders that assess shadow-object relations during detection.

papers.title: SDDNet: Style-guided Dual-layer Disentanglement Network for Shadow Detection
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 31st ACM International Conference on Multimedia
papers.key_idea: Single-image shadow detector that splits features into shadow and background layers to reduce errors on colored or complex backgrounds, at a reported 32 frames per second.
papers.method: Feature separation and recombination module plus a shadow style filter module.

papers.title: Fast Shadow Detection from a Single Image Using a Patched Convolutional Neural Network
papers.key_idea: Fast shadow detector: an SVM on statistical features gives a shadow prior map, then a semantic-aware patch-level CNN refines it, cutting time cost by one to two orders of magnitude.
papers.method: Multi-class SVM prior map from statistical features, then a patch-level CNN on the image plus the prior.

papers.title: FieldNet: Efficient Real-Time Shadow Removal for Enhanced Vision in Field Robotics
papers.key_idea: Shadow-removal network aimed at resource-constrained hardware that needs no shadow mask at inference; trained on natural images with synthetic shadows and shown to help weed detection in robot imagery.
papers.method: Probabilistic enhancement module and a new loss for inconsistent shadow-boundary supervision.

papers.title: Shadow detection: A survey and comparative evaluation of recent methods
papers.key_idea: Survey and comparison of moving cast-shadow detection methods grouped by cue (chromacity, physical, geometry, texture), proposing tracking performance as the yardstick for their practical usefulness.
papers.method: Feature-based taxonomy with quantitative and qualitative comparison of selected methods.

papers.title: Unveiling Deep Shadows: A Survey and Benchmark on Image and Video Shadow Detection, Removal, and Generation in the Deep Learning Era
papers.key_idea: Survey and re-trained benchmark of deep shadow detection, removal and generation for images and video; finds dataset bias and weak cross-dataset generalization, and points to geometry-aware and physics-guided priors.
papers.method: Taxonomy of architectures and supervision; representative methods re-trained under standardized settings.

papers.title: Benchmarking Adversarial Robustness of Image Shadow Removal with Shadow-adaptive Attacks
papers.key_idea: Shadow-adaptive adversarial attacks whose perturbation budget follows pixel intensity, used to benchmark how robust existing shadow-removal networks are on public datasets.
papers.method: Attack budget adjusted by local intensity so noise is less visible in shadowed regions; evaluation of existing removal methods under several attack levels.

papers.title: Exposing digital forgeries by detecting inconsistencies in lighting

papers.key_idea: Title only: photo-forensic test that exposes digital forgeries through inconsistencies in the lighting of a scene. Abstract not read; the estimation method and accuracy are UNVERIFIED here.

papers.title: Exposing photo manipulation with inconsistent shadows
papers.key_idea: Geometric test of whether cast and attached shadows in one image can come from a single point light source, posed as a linear program; no feasible solution is evidence of tampering.

papers.title: Using Expectation-Maximization for exposing image forgeries by revealing inconsistencies in shadow geometry
papers.venue: Journal of Visual Communication and Image Representation
papers.key_idea: Title only: image-forgery detection that uses expectation-maximization to reveal inconsistencies in shadow geometry. Abstract not read; data, accuracy and automation level are UNVERIFIED.

papers.title: What Do the Sun and the Sky Tell Us About the Camera?

papers.title: Solar position algorithm for solar radiation applications
papers.key_idea: Title only: published algorithm for computing the sun's position for solar radiation applications. Abstract not read; inputs, accuracy and cost are UNVERIFIED here.

papers.title: Shadow-Catcher: Looking into Shadows to Detect Ghost Objects in Autonomous Vehicle 3D Sensing

papers.key_idea: Title only: uses shadows in 3D sensing to detect ghost (spoofed) objects. The 2022 follow-up abstract calls 3D shadows a physical invariant for detecting fake objects.

papers.title: Using 3D Shadows to Detect Object Hiding Attacks on Autonomous Vehicle Perception
papers.key_idea: Finds obstacles hidden from LiDAR object detectors by searching point clouds for 3D shadows (regions with no measurements) and locating the object that causes each; a physical-invariant check against object-hiding attacks.

papers.title: Triple-cooperative Video Shadow Detection

papers.title: Revisiting Shadow Detection: A New Benchmark Dataset for Complex World
papers.key_idea: Compiles 10,500 shadow images with ground-truth masks across many scene categories, with varied shadow sizes, locations, contrasts and types, and adds a fast detection network with a detail-enhancement module.
papers.method: Dataset compilation and analysis plus a fast shadow detection network.

papers.title: Instance Shadow Detection with A Single-Stage Detector
papers.key_idea: Defines instance shadow detection (find each shadow and the object casting it), builds a dataset with shadow, object and association masks, a metric and a single-stage detector.
papers.method: Single-stage detector with a bidirectional relation learning module and a deformable mask-IoU head.

papers.title: Learning from Synthetic Shadows for Shadow Detection and Removal
papers.key_idea: Builds SynShadow, a large synthetic set of shadow, shadow-free and matte image triplets from a physically grounded shadow illumination model; pre-training on it improves shadow detection and removal models.

papers.title: LightCity: An Urban Dataset for Outdoor Inverse Rendering and Reconstruction under Multi-illumination Conditions
papers.key_idea: Synthetic urban dataset with controllable sky illumination and realistic indirect light and shadow effects, with depth, normals, materials and light properties, plus benchmarks of three tasks.

papers.title: Benchmarking the Robustness of Autonomous Driving to Environmental Illusions: A Lane Perception Perspective

papers.title: Shadow Transfer: Single Image Relighting For Urban Road Scenes

papers.title: Adversarial Neon Beam: A Light-based Physical Attack to DNNs

papers.title: Adversarial Color Projection: A Projector-based Physical Attack to DNNs
papers.key_idea: A projector casts optimised colour perturbations onto the target; success is judged on effectiveness, stealthiness and robustness against several DNNs.

papers.title: SLAP: Improving Physical Adversarial Examples with Short-Lived Adversarial Perturbations

papers.title: LaserGuider: A Laser Based Physical Backdoor Attack against Deep Neural Networks

papers.title: Invisible Reflections: Leveraging Infrared Laser Reflections to Target Traffic Sign Perception

papers.title: WIP: Infrared Laser Reflection Attack Against Traffic Sign Recognition Systems

papers.title: The Spectrum Strikes Back: Infrared POV Attacks on Traffic Sign Classification
