papers.method: Optimal display position found in digital simulation; physical tests with a Sony IMX708 module without infrared filter; detector finds saturated regions and checks for red and blue values above green nearby (sensor-specific).

papers.title: Targeted Physical Evasion Attacks in the Near-Infrared Domain
papers.venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium (NDSS)
papers.key_idea: An off-the-shelf infrared flashlight shines a transparent-film pattern onto a sign, giving targeted and untargeted infrared perturbations without lasers; a Segment-Anything shape-count detector flags the added edges.
papers.method: Film-projected infrared transformation optimised digitally and replayed physically; detector counts Segment Anything (ViT-L) masks and thresholds the count.

papers.title: Invisible Optical Adversarial Stripes on Traffic Sign against Autonomous Vehicles
papers.venue: ACM International Conference on Mobile Systems, Applications and Services (MobiSys)
papers.key_idea: Modulated LED light exploits the camera rolling shutter to paint stripes on a sign that people cannot see; the emission timing adapts to camera operation and vehicle motion so recognition stays wrong across frames.
papers.method: GhostStripe controls the timing of modulated light emission relative to the rolling-shutter readout; countermeasures are discussed at sensor, model and system level.

papers.title: The Fluorescent Veil: A Stealthy and Effective Physical Adversarial Patch Against Traffic Sign Recognition
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
papers.key_idea: Fluorescent ink on a sign is triggered by invisible ultraviolet light, producing a perturbation that misleads traffic sign recognition; the attack is modelled digitally to pick optimal fluorescence settings.
papers.method: Digital model of the fluorescence effect to choose settings; physical patch triggered by ultraviolet light.

papers.title: Detecting and Identifying Optical Signal Attacks on Autonomous Driving Systems
papers.key_idea: With three sensors the framework builds two disparity maps and flags optical attacks from the distribution of disparity errors; an identification model then finds which sensor is attacked.
papers.method: Two depth versions from three sensors; distribution analysis of disparity errors; identification scheme with a correctness proof for up to n-2 attacked sensors (one LiDAR, n cameras).

papers.title: WIP: Adversarial Retroreflective Patches: A Novel Stealthy Attack on Traffic Sign Recognition at Night
papers.venue: Symposium on Vehicle Security and Privacy (VehicleSec)
papers.key_idea: Retroreflective patches matching the sign colour are inconspicuous by day and return headlight light to the camera at night, disturbing sign recognition; preliminary feasibility study with digital and physical tests.
papers.method: Digital simulation of the reflection by image processing, then physical patches on a real sign photographed under headlights; YOLOv3-tiny as target.

papers.title: Trapped by Their Own Light: Deployable and Stealth Retroreflective Patch Attacks on Traffic Sign Recognition Systems
papers.key_idea: Retroreflective patches in the sign colour stay hidden by day and return headlight light at night, misleading recognition; a polarizing-filter defence (DPR Shield) on headlight and camera suppresses the patch return.
papers.method: Physics-based retroreflection simulation in Blender (roughness, IoR level, specular tint fitted to measurements), black-box patch optimisation, physical tests with a FLIR Blackfly S camera; defence uses a polarised headlight with a crossed camera filter.

papers.title: Reflective Adversarial Attacks against Pedestrian Detection Systems for Vehicles at Night
papers.key_idea: Reflective microprism patches matching clothing colour are placed by particle swarm search; at night, headlight return disrupts vehicle pedestrian detectors; a symmetry strategy uses a surrogate model for black-box transfer.
papers.method: Particle swarm patch placement on YOLOv5-generated examples; deployment on clothing with 3M DG3 reflective sheeting; night tests with vehicles passing at several distances.

papers.title: Physics-Based Adversarial Attack on Near-Infrared Human Detector for Nighttime Surveillance Camera Systems
papers.venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
papers.key_idea: Night-mode surveillance cameras with the IR-cut filter off see near-infrared images where clothing loses colour and texture; retro-reflective and insulating tapes form patterns that hide a person from a YOLO detector.
papers.method: Binary tape patterns designed digitally by black-box query and search, then realised with retro-reflective and electrical-insulation tapes on clothes.

papers.title: Rolling Colors: Adversarial Laser Exploits against Traffic Light Recognition
papers.key_idea: Modulated laser pulses exploit the rolling shutter to inject a colour stripe over a traffic light; the paper catalogues laser effects on images: overexposure, colour shift, stripes, white-balance shift and defocus.
papers.method: Optimisation of laser parameters from empirical interference models; emulated and real set-ups; countermeasure proposed: randomised rolling-shutter row order.

papers.title: State-of-the-art optical-based physical adversarial attacks for deep learning computer vision systems
papers.key_idea: Survey of optical (light-irradiation) physical adversarial attacks on vision systems, placed in the non-invasive class of attacks that resemble natural lighting effects and are hard for people to notice.
papers.method: Literature review; physical attacks divided into invasive and non-invasive.

papers.title: Single-Image Reflection Removal Using Deep Learning: A Systematic Review
papers.key_idea: Systematic review of deep-learning single-image reflection removal; shows that most work evaluates on the SIR2 benchmark and on real-world data rather than on synthetic data only.
papers.method: Systematic literature review with research questions; RQ3 covers datasets.

papers.title: Benchmarking Single-Image Reflection Removal Algorithms
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
papers.key_idea: Taxonomy and benchmark of single-image reflection removal: the SIR2+ dataset adds in-the-wild scenes and coloured or non-planar glass, with unified quantitative comparisons of learning-based methods.
papers.method: Analysis of reflection properties, a taxonomy, a new dataset and unified benchmarking of state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Survey on Single-Image Reflection Removal Using Deep Learning Techniques
papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Multimedia Information Processing and Retrieval (MIPR)
papers.key_idea: Survey of 28 deep single-image reflection removal papers from major venues with datasets, metrics and challenges; notes that small U-Net style models already reach state-of-the-art because data are scarce.
papers.method: Structured paper selection (2017-2025) and critical review of single-stage and two-stage methods.

papers.title: A Multi-Task Network for Joint Specular Highlight Detection and Removal
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: A new dataset of about 16K real images with highlight detection and removal ground truth, and a multi-task network that detects and removes highlights from one specular image-formation model.
papers.method: Multi-task network built on a new specular highlight image formation model; trained on real rather than synthetic data to close the domain gap.

papers.title: Joint specular highlight detection and removal in single images via Unet-Transformer
papers.key_idea: Two branches: a plain U-Net encoder-decoder detects highlight masks, then a Swin-transformer U-Net removes the highlights, guided by the mask; trained and tested on SHIQ images.
papers.method: Mask detection branch with four down-sampling layers; Swin-transformer U-Net removal branch; joint training.

papers.title: SpecSeg Network for Specular Highlight Detection and Segmentation in Real-World Images
papers.key_idea: U-Net based specular pixel segmentation for indoor and outdoor images, trained on public datasets; authors report sky, puddles and large white areas of road signs or car bodies were not falsely marked.
papers.method: U-Net encoder-decoder segmentation of specular pixels; quick to train on nominal-sized datasets (abstract).

papers.title: Shift-Window Meets Dual Attention: A Multi-Model Architecture for Specular Highlight Removal
papers.key_idea: Multi-model highlight removal network with convolutions in shallow layers and shifted-window plus dual attention in deep layers; compared with five other methods on FLOPs and parameters.
papers.method: Coarse-to-fine removal with omnidirectional attention integration and region-aware hybrid-domain attention blocks; frequency processing at several scales.

papers.title: UnReflectAnything: RGB-Only Highlight Removal by Rendering Synthetic Specular Supervision
papers.key_idea: RGB-only highlight removal: a frozen vision-transformer encoder, a lightweight head that localises specular regions and a token-level inpainting module; trained with rendered synthetic highlights.
papers.method: Virtual Highlight Synthesis renders specularities from monocular geometry, Fresnel-aware shading and random lighting; predicts a highlight map and a diffuse image.

papers.title: Let The Sunshine in: Sun Glare Detection on Automotive Surround-view Cameras
papers.venue: Electronic Imaging (IS&T Autonomous Vehicles and Machines)
papers.key_idea: Sun glare detection for automotive surround-view cameras with two complementary methods, classical image processing and a CNN; builds a WoodScape glare dataset covering road, water, signs, cars and direct sun.
papers.method: Classical image-processing filters combined with multi-camera tracking, and a fully convolutional network trained on the new glare set; annotations from automatic thresholding followed by manual checks.

papers.title: Robust Glare Detection: Review, Analysis, and Dataset Release
papers.key_idea: Glare appears under sun, night lights and reflective surfaces and depends on camera shutter and exposure; the paper releases a multi-camera glare detection dataset and tests image representations in a deep network.
papers.method: Review of glare, analysis of image representations and their combinations, a deep detection network.

papers.title: How to deal with glare for improved perception of Autonomous Vehicles
papers.key_idea: Compares glare reduction techniques, including a proposed saturated-pixel-aware method, by their effect on object detection, recognition, tracking, depth estimation and lane detection in autonomous driving.
papers.method: Glare reduction as a pre-processing step; evaluation through the downstream perception tasks.

papers.title: Fundaments in Luminance and Retroreflectivity Measurements of Vertical Traffic Signs Using a Color Digital Camera
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
papers.key_idea: Relates camera pixel values to luminance and retroreflectivity of vertical traffic signs; with a photometrically calibrated camera, retroreflectivity stayed constant with distance under fixed and headlamp-like lighting.
papers.method: Photometric camera calibration; derivation of luminance and retroreflectivity from pixel value, exposure, aperture and light-source geometry (incidence and emission angles).

papers.title: A comprehensive survey of specularity detection: state-of-the-art techniques and breakthroughs
papers.key_idea: Survey of specularity detection techniques; the article page defines specularity as reflective phenomena on mirrors, polished metals, water and reflective regions of objects (scope sentence only; abstract not read).

papers.title: NRGS-Net: A Lightweight Uformer with Gated Positional and Local Context Attention for Nighttime Road Glare Suppression
papers.key_idea: Lightweight Uformer variant with gated positional attention suppresses glare, glow and flare from streetlights and headlights in night road images; releases the Night Road Glare Dataset.
papers.method: Gated positional attention module, depthwise separable convolutions in down-sampling, residual PixelShuffle up-sampling, channel attention in the feed-forward block.

papers.title: Remote Perception Attacks against Camera-based Object Recognition Systems and Countermeasures
papers.key_idea: Projector patterns exploit lens-flare ghosts and auto-exposure; the countermeasure flags a ghost overlapping a detected object and uses two frames from a moving camera to reject natural light sources.
papers.method: Ghost positions computed from the lens configuration (white-box) and a detected light source; alarm when a ghost lies within a distance threshold of a detected object; spatiotemporal consistency over two frames removes false positives from sun or streetlights.

papers.title: Revisiting Physical-World Adversarial Attack on Traffic Sign Recognition: A Commercial Systems Perspective
papers.key_idea: Large-scale measurement of physical-world attacks on commercial traffic sign recognition: success is often much lower than reported for academic models, partly because of a spatial memorization design; new system-level attack success metrics are proposed.
papers.method: Measurement on commercial recognition systems; metrics that model the effect of spatial memorization on system-level success; re-evaluation of existing attacks.

papers.title: SentiNet: Detecting Localized Universal Attacks Against Deep Learning Systems
papers.key_idea: Detection framework for localized universal attacks that needs no training and no prior knowledge of the attack, using model interpretability and object detection techniques; tested on poisoning, trojans and adversarial patches.
papers.method: Interpretability-based localisation of the regions that drive a prediction, combined with object-detection techniques; no detector training.

papers.title: Blinded by the Beam: A Unified Real-Time Defense Against Laser-Based Attacks on Navigational Perception of Autonomous Vehicles
papers.key_idea: Static-parameter versions of AdvLB and AdvLS are analysed; a lightweight unified detector combines image statistics, filters (sharpening, Laplacian), HSV contour extraction and geometric cues, reaching over 90% detection accuracy on a Jetson Orin Nano.
papers.method: First-order statistics, sharpening and Laplacian filters and HSV-based contour extraction for AdvLB-like streaks; geometry-aware adaptive methods for the subtler AdvLS spots; machine-learning anomaly detection.

papers.title: Road scenes analysis in adverse weather conditions by polarization-encoded images and adapted deep learning
papers.key_idea: Polarimetric camera images, used instead of RGB with fine-tuned RetinaNet and SSD, improve car and person detection in adverse weather and strong reflections; an RGB camera beside it allows same-scene testing.
papers.method: Polarisation channel combinations (I0/I45/I135, Stokes S0-S2, S0/AoP/DoP) fed to detectors after fine-tuning; no data augmentation because it breaks the physical meaning.

papers.title: Polarimetric Imaging for Perception
papers.key_idea: RGB-polarimetric camera compared with RGB for monocular depth and free-space detection at midday; adds a dataset of RGB-polarimetric images with lidar, GNSS/IMU and free-space masks; polarisation depends on viewing direction.
papers.method: Standard networks with minimal changes for RGB-only, polarimetric-only and combined inputs; study limited to midday, when polarisation does not depend on heading.

papers.title: Generic and real-time detection of specular reflections in images
papers.venue: International Conference on Computer Vision Theory and Applications (VISAPP)
papers.key_idea: Real-time specular highlight detector in HSV space: low-saturation, high-value thresholds, contrast adaptation for lighting jumps, and a gradient-based step that rejects bright white regions.
papers.method: Automatic Value threshold from image brightness (fitted on 50 images), constant Saturation threshold, contrast reduction when brightness is too high, region-wise gradient test to drop false detections; complexity O(n + k*c).

papers.title: Natural Light Can Also Be Dangerous: Traffic Sign Misinterpretation Under Adversarial Natural Light Attacks
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
papers.key_idea: Simulates sunlight, headlight and flashlight illumination and searches, with a black-box zeroth-order method, for light patterns in a physically reproducible space that make sign models misclassify while looking like natural light.
papers.method: Zeroth-order optimisation (ZOO) in a physically applicable space of simulated light sources; adversarial training with the generated samples as a mitigation.

papers.title: Phantom of the ADAS: Securing Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems from Split-Second Phantom Attacks
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 2020 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security
papers.key_idea: Depthless phantom objects shown for a split second, by projector or billboard video, are treated as real by two commercial driver-assistance systems; a camera-only committee of CNNs checks object light, context, surface and depth.
papers.method: Field tests on a Tesla Model X and a Mobileye 630; countermeasure GhostBusters: four lightweight CNNs (light, context, surface, depth) judge the cropped detected object and their outputs are combined.

papers.title: They See Me Rollin’: Inherent Vulnerability of the Rolling Shutter in CMOS Image Sensors
papers.key_idea: A bright modulated light, even a cheap laser, injects fine stripes via the rolling shutter of CMOS cameras; stripe size is modelled from datasheet values, and a lightweight detector enhancement is proposed.
papers.method: Attack on seven CMOS cameras; model of attack parameters validated on two cameras; object-detection evaluation; lightweight addition to the detector backbone to recognise rolling-shutter attacks.

papers.title: Invisible Perturbations: Physical Adversarial Examples Exploiting the Rolling Shutter Effect
papers.venue: 2021 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Instead of marking the object, the attacker modulates the illuminating light; the rolling shutter of ordinary cameras turns this into stripes that mislead an ImageNet classifier while the scene looks evenly lit to people.
papers.method: Craft a temporal light signal that exploits the radiometric rolling-shutter effect; simulation plus physical experiments with LEDs.

papers.title: Invisible Optical Adversarial Stripes on Traffic Sign against Autonomous Vehicles
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 22nd Annual International Conference on Mobile Systems, Applications and Services
papers.key_idea: LEDs flickering at timed intervals create stripes on a traffic sign through the camera rolling shutter; GhostStripe adapts emission timing to the camera and the moving vehicle so the wrong class persists over frames.
papers.method: Vehicle tracking and camera-timing control of the LED modulation; real testbeds; countermeasures discussed at camera-sensor, perception-model and driving-system levels.

papers.title: Invisible Adversarial Stripes on Traffic Sign: Threat and Defense for Autonomous Vehicles
papers.key_idea: Extends the GhostStripe attack with GhostBuster, a software module that detects stripe perturbations on the sign and restores the sign natural look before recognition.
papers.method: Software defence made of a perturbation detector and a sign restorer; other camera-sensor and system-level countermeasures are discussed.

papers.title: L-HAWK: A Controllable Physical Adversarial Patch Against a Long-Distance Target
papers.venue: Proceedings 2025 Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
papers.key_idea: A printed adversarial patch stays harmless until a long-distance laser hitting the target vehicle camera creates a translucent colour strip that triggers the patch, so only chosen vehicles are affected.
papers.method: The laser-created colour strip in the image acts as the trigger; the patch is built to cause stop-sign misrecognition only when the strip is present (talk description).

papers.title: GhostImage: Remote Perception Attacks against Camera-based Image Classification Systems
papers.key_idea: A low-cost projector remotely injects adversarial patterns into a camera by exploiting lens flare and ghost effects and auto-exposure control, creating spurious or altered objects for the classifier.
papers.method: Adversarial patterns optimised together with a trained end-to-end channel model of the projector-to-camera path; three cameras and three image datasets, indoors and outdoors.

papers.title: Optical Adversarial Attack
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)
papers.key_idea: A low-cost projector-camera system alters an object appearance with structured illumination; a projector-camera model is built into the attack optimisation so attacks work despite non-linear projector response and background light.
papers.method: Attack formulation that includes the radiometric projector-camera model; white-box, black-box, targeted and untargeted attacks on image classifiers; theoretical analysis of the performance limit.

papers.title: Transient Adversarial 3D Projection Attacks on Object Detection in Autonomous Driving
papers.key_idea: Projected adversarial patches on 3D curved surfaces such as vehicles, built from colour-mapping and geometric-transformation models, fool YOLOv3 and Mask R-CNN and are strongest when ambient light is low.
papers.method: Optimisation with a colour-mapping model and a geometric-transformation model; physical indoor tests with a projector at varying distance, angle and ambient light.

papers.title: Adversarial Laser Beam: Effective Physical-World Attack to DNNs in a Blink
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: A laser beam whose physical parameters (for example wavelength and width) are optimised serves as the perturbation; it can be switched on in a blink just before capture and also works at night.
papers.method: Optimisation of laser-beam physical parameters against image classifiers in digital and physical settings.

papers.title: Over-the-Air Adversarial Flickering Attacks against Video Recognition Networks
papers.venue: 2021 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: A temporal flickering perturbation fools video action classifiers, can be made universal and synchronisation-free, and is demonstrated over the air; in some cases it is unnoticeable to observers.
papers.method: Optimised temporal perturbation applied as scene illumination flicker; universal and temporal-invariant variants; transfer tested on several target models.

papers.title: Imperceptible Physical Attack against Face Recognition Systems via LED Illumination Modulation
papers.key_idea: Fast intensity modulation of scene LEDs gives luminance changes invisible to people; the rolling shutter turns them into perturbations in captured face images, causing detection denial and verification dodging.
papers.method: LED illumination modulation exploiting the CMOS rolling shutter; tested on face detectors (Dlib, MTCNN, RetinaFace) and verifiers (Dlib, FaceNet, ArcFace).

papers.title: A Dataset for Provident Vehicle Detection at Night
papers.key_idea: 59,746 annotated grayscale night images from 346 rural scenes, labelling oncoming vehicles, their headlamps and light reflections on guardrails, to study detecting vehicles from the light they cause.
papers.method: Open-source dataset with vehicle, light-object and light-reflection labels, plus first benchmark results with state-of-the-art and custom detectors.

papers.title: ACDC: The Adverse Conditions Dataset with Correspondences for Robust Semantic Driving Scene Perception
papers.key_idea: 8,012 driving images, half equally split over fog, night, rain and snow, each adverse image paired with a normal-condition image of the same scene and pixel-level panoptic labels.
papers.method: Public benchmark for semantic, instance and panoptic segmentation, object detection and uncertainty-aware segmentation under adverse conditions.

papers.title: Getting to Know Low-light Images with The Exclusively Dark Dataset
papers.key_idea: Ten types of low-light images (low, ambient, object, single, weak, strong, screen, window, shadow, twilight) with image and object-level labels; the authors find low-light effects run deeper than simple illumination invariance can fix.
papers.method: Exclusively low-light dataset captured in visible light; analysis of hand-crafted and learned features for object detection under low light.

papers.title: Flare7K: A Phenomenological Nighttime Flare Removal Dataset
papers.key_idea: Synthetic nighttime lens-flare dataset: 5,000 scattering and 2,000 reflective flare images (25 plus 10 types), with annotations for light source, glare, reflective flare and streak, for flare-corrupted and clean pairs.
papers.method: Flare patterns generated from observation and statistics of real nighttime flares and composited onto flare-free images to train removal networks.

papers.title: Flare7K++: Mixing Synthetic and Real Datasets for Nighttime Flare Removal and Beyond
papers.key_idea: Adds 962 real-captured nighttime flare images (Flare-R) to the 7,000 synthetic flares, annotates light sources, and proposes a pipeline that removes flare while preserving the light source.
papers.method: Mixed synthetic and real flare data; end-to-end pipeline that keeps the light source while removing lens flare.

papers.title: NightOwls: A Pedestrians at Night Dataset
papers.key_idea: Pedestrian detection dataset recorded at night (from the title only; abstract not read).
papers.method: Not read.

papers.title: Autonomous Vehicles Camera Blinding Attack Detection Using Sequence Modelling and Predictive Analytics
papers.key_idea: Detects camera blinding by projected light: a convolutional encoder-decoder predicts the next video frame, and an attack is flagged when similarity between predicted and received frame falls below a fixed threshold.
papers.method: Sequence model for next-frame prediction; similarity between predicted and incoming frame; fixed-threshold decision.

papers.title: AdvRain: Adversarial Raindrops to Attack Camera-Based Smart Vision Systems
papers.key_idea: Raindrop-like blur patterns printed on a translucent sticker over the camera lens mislead camera-based perception while passing as natural rain; critical positions come from a random search.
papers.method: Iterative random search for critical positions; blurring of image regions covered by printed drops; sticker placed over the lens when the attack is triggered.

papers.title: Neural Auto-Exposure for High-Dynamic Range Object Detection
papers.venue: 2021 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Learned auto-exposure control aimed at object detection in high-dynamic-range scenes (from the title only; abstract not read).
papers.method: Not read.

papers.title: MLIA: modulated LED illumination-based adversarial attack on traffic sign recognition system for autonomous vehicle
papers.venue: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Trust, Security and Privacy in Computing and Communications (TrustCom)
papers.key_idea: Attack on traffic sign recognition that uses modulated LED illumination (from the title only; abstract not read).
papers.method: Not read.

papers.title: Light Projection-Based Physical-World Vanishing Attack Against Car Detection
papers.venue: ICASSP 2023 - 2023 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
papers.key_idea: A projected adversarial light pattern makes a detector miss a car; a 2024 review describes a drone-borne portable projector aimed at the rear windshield (secondary description).
papers.method: Light projection onto a vehicle to cause a vanishing (miss) attack on car detection (title and secondary description).

papers.title: Visual Adversarial Attacks and Defenses in the Physical World: A Survey
papers.key_idea: Survey of physical adversarial attacks and defences in computer vision, with a taxonomy by attack task, form and method, and defences grouped as pre-processing, in-processing and post-processing.
papers.method: Literature survey and taxonomy.

papers.title: Automotive 8.3 MP CMOS Image Sensor with 150 dB Dynamic Range and Light Flicker Mitigation
papers.key_idea: Automotive image sensor with very high dynamic range and built-in light flicker mitigation, a sensor-level answer to LED flicker (from the title only; abstract not read).
papers.method: Sensor design (not read).

papers.title: A 0.68e-rms Random-Noise 121dB Dynamic-Range Sub-pixel architecture CMOS Image Sensor with LED Flicker Mitigation
papers.key_idea: Sub-pixel CMOS sensor design with high dynamic range and LED flicker mitigation, an earlier sensor-level treatment of LED flicker (from the title only; abstract not read).
papers.method: Sensor design (not read).

papers.title: DiffuFlicker: Diffusion-Based LED Traffic Light Flicker Removal in Dashcam Videos
papers.key_idea: Diffusion-based removal of LED traffic-light flicker from dashcam video (from the title only; abstract not read).
papers.method: Not read.

papers.title: Adversarial color projection: A projector-based physical-world attack to DNNs
papers.key_idea: Physical-world attack that projects colour onto the scene to mislead DNNs (from the title only; abstract not read).
papers.method: Not read.

papers.title: CausalAttack: Real-time Light-based Physical Adversarial Attack via Interpretable Causal Reasoning for DNNs
papers.key_idea: Real-time attack that manipulates light conditions (project-and-capture) using causal reasoning, a learned approximation of the project-and-capture step, and an expectation-over-transformation tuned to brightness and projection noise.
papers.method: Plug-in project-and-capture approximation built on a large vision-language model with incremental learning; causal reasoning for interpretable adversarial texture; transformation model for brightness and projection noise.

papers.title: Adversarial Camera Patch: An Effective and Robust Physical-World Attack on Object Detectors
papers.venue: International Conference on Cyber Warfare and Security
papers.key_idea: A patch attached to the camera lens, with width and transparency tuned by particle swarm optimisation, yields stealthy adversarial samples against object detectors, validated digitally and physically.
papers.method: Particle swarm optimisation of the physical parameters of a lens patch; ablations in a digital environment; physical tests.

papers.title: AdvLensPolluter: Object-oriented Adversarial Camera Contamination Attack
papers.venue: 2025 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
papers.key_idea: Attack that contaminates the camera lens to target chosen objects (from the title only; abstract not read).
papers.method: Not read.

papers.title: Lens Flare-Aware Detector in Autonomous Driving
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 19th International Joint Conference on Computer Vision, Imaging and Computer Graphics Theory and Applications
papers.key_idea: Object detector made aware of lens flare in autonomous-driving images (from the title only; abstract not read).
papers.method: Not read.

papers.title: Joint Characterization of PWM Headlight and Event Camera Bias Parameters for Nighttime Object Detection
papers.key_idea: Study of PWM-driven LED headlight flicker and event-camera bias settings for nighttime object detection (from the title only; abstract not read).
papers.method: Not read.

papers.title: Transient Deception: Recent Advances and Trends in Short-Lived Adversarial Examples
papers.key_idea: Survey and taxonomy of short-lived adversarial examples covering flickering-based, motion-based, sensor-based, projection-based and gradient-based perturbations, split by white-box versus black-box, targeted, physical versus digital, and persistent versus short-lived.
papers.method: Literature survey and taxonomy.

papers.title: Laser Guard: Efficiently Detecting Laser-Based Physical Adversarial Attacks in Autonomous Driving
papers.key_idea: Detector for laser-based physical adversarial attacks in autonomous driving, described in the title as efficient (title only; abstract not read).
papers.method: Not read.

papers.title: AdvIT: Adversarial Frames Identifier Based on Temporal Consistency in Videos
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
papers.key_idea: Detects adversarial frames by rebuilding a pseudo frame from the previous frame with optical flow and checking whether the model output on the target frame agrees with the output on the pseudo frame.
papers.method: Optical-flow warping of the previous frame to a pseudo frame; inconsistency score between learner outputs on target and pseudo frame; thresholded.

papers.title: Identifying and Resisting Adversarial Videos Using Temporal Consistency
papers.key_idea: Flags adversarial videos by counting frames whose predicted label differs from both neighbours (exception index), then repairs sparse polluted frames by temporal reconstruction and dense ones with a spatial denoiser.
papers.method: Per-frame labels from a CNN+LSTM classifier without recurrent links; exception index against two thresholds; temporal or spatial defense depending on the attack density.

papers.title: Real-Time Detectors for Digital and Physical Adversarial Inputs to Perception Systems
papers.key_idea: Flags an input as attacked when the classifier output changes strongly after a label-preserving transformation; light enough for real time; also releases AdvNet, clean and physically attacked traffic sign images.
papers.method: Compare classifier outputs on the input and on a transformed copy; threshold; designed to be attack- and dataset-agnostic.

papers.title: Real-Time Robust Video Object Detection System Against Physical-World Adversarial Attacks
papers.key_idea: Defends video detection against adversarial patches by finding small regions of very localized feature importance with non-robust predictions; examines key frames and predicts the patch region in other frames from optical flow.
papers.method: Adversarial region detection on key frames; computer-vision or DNN optical flow to propagate the region; software and hardware co-design to cut redundant computation.

papers.title: AD2: Analysis and Detection of Adversarial Threats in Visual Perception for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Systems
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
papers.key_idea: Lightweight attention detector on consecutive multi-camera frame pairs that captures spatial-temporal consistency to separate benign frames from blur, electromagnetic-interference and ghost-object attacks in CARLA closed-loop driving.
papers.method: Pair of three-camera frames at t-1 and t; four-way classification (benign and three attacks); compared with focus measure, kernel PCA and a ResNet detector.

papers.title: Attention-Based Real-Time Defenses for Physical Adversarial Attacks in Vision Applications
papers.venue: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Cyber-Physical Systems (ICCPS)
papers.key_idea: Uses adversarial channel attention in shallow layers to find and track malicious objects across frames and mask their effect, aiming at multi-frame real-time decisions at low computational cost.
papers.method: Over-activation of channel attention localizes the patch; the region is tracked over frames and masked; defense quality and computational cost are both evaluated.

papers.title: That Person Moves Like A Car: Misclassification Attack Detection for Autonomous Systems Using Spatiotemporal Consistency
papers.key_idea: Cross-checks the class an object detector gives a track against the spatiotemporal properties of that track and against context such as ego velocity, without assuming how the perturbation was made.
papers.method: Consistency check between track-derived features and class prediction (PercepGuard), plus a contextual check that raises the cost of adaptive attacks.

papers.title: AdROD: HyperNetwork-based Adversarially Robust Object Detection for Autonomous Driving
papers.key_idea: Ensemble defense whose on-demand mode tracks objects with a Kalman filter, flags abrupt vanishing, waits three frames in a watch set, then activates the ensemble or warns that recovery failed.
papers.method: AdROD-I: per-frame low-rank HyperNetwork ensemble with input transforms and disagreement-based recovery. AdROD-II: Kalman state per object, abrupt-disappearance test from the box-scale trend, watch set with a 3-frame extrapolation window, early-terminating ensemble.

papers.title: VisionGuard: Secure and Robust Visual Perception of Autonomous Vehicles in Practice
papers.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
papers.key_idea: Predicts the ego vehicle motion from past GPS and IMU states (Kalman filter, ARIMA) and runs a Normal, Warning, Attack state machine on accumulated prediction residuals to detect physical attacks.
papers.method: Corrected driving state; short and long-term predictions; two residual thresholds open a Warning interval; an accumulated residual above a threshold inside it raises Attack, otherwise the state returns to Normal.

papers.title: PhySense: Defending Physically Realizable Attacks for Autonomous Systems via Consistency Reasoning
papers.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
papers.key_idea: Recovers correct labels under physical attacks by reasoning over objects and their relations as a spatial-temporal conditional random field built from physical attributes, with cross-frame consistency to save compute.
papers.method: CRF over a spatial-temporal graph of objects using static and dynamic physical features and a 3D kinematic model; costly inference only on new or attacked objects; pipelined implementation.

papers.title: Physics-Aware Spatiotemporal Consistency for Transferable Defense of Autonomous Driving Perception
papers.key_idea: Compares a class distribution inferred from appearance with one inferred from kinematics (frequency-domain trajectory embedding) using a symmetric KL energy; above a threshold it trusts the motion-based class.
papers.method: Trained dual-stream spatiotemporal encoder on detector backbone features, outputs and tracking states; TAME energy; threshold 0.2 chosen to keep benign false positives below 5 percent; plug-in behind several detectors.

papers.title: PhyScout: Detecting Sensor Spoofing Attacks via Spatio-temporal Consistency
papers.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
papers.key_idea: Detects sensor spoofing, including camera adversarial patches, by defining the spatio-temporal conflicts such attacks cause between observed keypoints and vehicle state predicted with a state-space model.
papers.method: Generalized spatio-temporal conflict definitions; matching of keypoints against predicted state; thresholds set from repeated normal and attacked runs (PDF extract).

papers.title: ADC: Adversarial attacks against object Detection that evade Context consistency checks
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
papers.key_idea: Shows context-consistency checks can be bypassed: a joint optimization fools the detector while keeping object relationships plausible, in white-box and gray-box variants.
papers.method: Joint objective: detector-fooling loss plus terms that satisfy the context-consistency checker.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Consistency: A Universal Defense Against Attacks on Autonomous Systems
papers.key_idea: Short overview grouping perception attacks (misclassification, object deletion or creation, tracker hijacking, sensor spoofing) and how spatiotemporal and contextual consistency defenses exploit them; lists limits and adaptive attacks.
papers.method: Perspective article; no new experiments.

papers.title: A Certifiable Security Patch for Object Tracking in Self-Driving Systems via Historical Deviation Modeling
papers.key_idea: Keeps a buffer of past observation-versus-prediction deviations and clips abnormal deviations to a quantile bound inside Kalman-filter trackers, certifiably limiting how far a hijacking attack can drag a track.
papers.method: Outlier-aware deviation buffer, per-axis Gamma fit, clipping at the 95 percent quantile that stays silent for normal deviations; analytical bound on the attack effect.

papers.title: DetectorGuard: Provably Securing Object Detectors against Localized Patch Hiding Attacks
papers.key_idea: Checks that a normal detector's boxes explain objectness predicted by a provably robust classifier; unexplained objectness raises an attack alert, and certified objects are either detected or alerted.
papers.method: Robust image classifier adapted to predict objectness per location, explained by the conventional detector output; alert when objectness is unexplained.

papers.title: Fooling Detection Alone is Not Enough: First Adversarial Attack against Multiple Object Tracking
papers.key_idea: Tracker hijacking: adversarial examples on the detector in as few as one to three frames shift a tracked box so that an object appears to move into or out of the vehicle's path.
papers.method: Perturbs detector outputs in a few frames to pull a Kalman-filter based multiple-object-tracking track away (move-in and move-out scenarios).

papers.title: Physical Hijacking Attacks against Object Trackers
papers.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)
papers.key_idea: Physical-world attacks that hijack object trackers (move-in and move-out of an object track), evaluated on the VOT dataset and CARLA, using valid scene surfaces as the attack area.
papers.method: Hijacking attack on tracking-by-detection pipelines; details beyond figure captions and keywords not read.

papers.title: ControlLoc: Physical-World Hijacking Attack on Visual Perception in Autonomous Driving
papers.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS) 2025 (arXiv 2406.05810)
papers.key_idea: Physical patch attack on detection plus tracking: first picks the best patch location, then crafts a patch that shifts the perceived position and shape of objects to hijack the tracker.
papers.method: Two stages: patch location search, then patch generation that alters detected box location and shape; aware that tracking needs consistent detections over several frames.

papers.title: Physical ID-Transfer Attacks against Multi-Object Tracking via Adversarial Trajectory
papers.key_idea: Online physical attack on tracking-by-detection trackers that moves an adversary along a crafted trajectory so its tracker ID transfers to a targeted object, without attacking the detector.
papers.method: Adversarial trajectories against the association step of SORT-style trackers; two universal manoeuvres a person or driver can perform.

papers.title: SlowPerception: Physical-World Latency Attack against Visual Perception in Autonomous Driving

papers.method: Projector-based universal perturbation optimized to raise the number of boxes and trackers, which increases NMS and MOT computation.

papers.title: Towards Powerful and Practical Patch Attacks for 2D Object Detection in Autonomous Driving
papers.key_idea: Black-box transferable patch attack with a stricter practical success metric (PASR) and a physical test that measures how long a pedestrian stays undetected in video.
papers.method: Localization-confidence suppression loss and scale-preserving padding for high-resolution data; reports the longest continuous run of missed detections.

papers.title: Adversarial Tracking: Attacks on Image Sensors for Object Tracking in Autonomous Vehicles
papers.key_idea: Evaluates image-specific and image-agnostic attacks on YOLOv3 and YOLOv4 paired with four SORT-family trackers in CARLA and reports the damage in tracking metrics instead of detection accuracy.
papers.method: Attack-and-track evaluation with MOTA, HOTA and IDF1.

papers.title: Explainable Deep Anomaly Detection with Sequential Hypothesis Testing for Robotic Sewer Inspection
papers.key_idea: Adds a sequential probability ratio test on top of a per-frame anomaly detector so evidence accumulates over frames; frames between the two thresholds stay undecided.
papers.method: Single-frame anomaly scores feed an SPRT; log-likelihood ratio accumulated over frames; decision thresholds set from alpha and beta.

papers.title: Adaptive Multi-Mode Out-of-Distribution Detection for Trajectory Prediction in Autonomous Vehicles
papers.key_idea: Mode-aware CUSUM monitors trajectory-prediction errors, identifies the active error mode and adapts thresholds, lowering detection delay and false alarms against single-distribution CUSUM.
papers.method: Classical CUSUM log-likelihood accumulation extended to several error modes; threshold calibrated to a mean-time-to-false-alarm constraint (text extract).

papers.title: Sequential (Quickest) Change Detection: Classical Results and New Directions
papers.key_idea: Survey of online (quickest) change detection: the basics, generalizations, intersections with other areas and applications, including detecting attacks in streaming data.
papers.method: Theory survey.

papers.title: Memoryless Cumulative Sign Detector for Stealthy CPS Sensor Attacks
papers.key_idea: Memoryless run-time monitor that counts sign changes of measurement residuals to catch stealthy falsified sensor data, combined with CUSUM for magnitude bounds, without storing long sequences.
papers.method: Cumulative sign statistic on residuals following the chi-squared scheme; augmented with CUSUM.

papers.title: Detecting Object Tracking Failure via Sequential Hypothesis Testing
papers.key_idea: Treats tracking reliability as a sequential test: an e-process accumulates evidence that tracking quality fell below a tolerance and alarms when it crosses a threshold, with provably bounded false alerts.
papers.method: E-process (testing by betting) over a bounded per-frame tracking metric; alarm threshold 1/alpha from Ville inequality; supervised and unsupervised variants; no extra training.

papers.title: Real-time detection of deception attacks in cyber-physical systems
papers.key_idea: Inductive conformal anomaly detection with a generative model (VAE plus RNN) scores camera-observation sequences against normal behaviour; a CUSUM on the resulting p-values raises the alarm for deception attacks.
papers.method: VAE and RNN predict several future observations; nonconformity of the sequence gives p-values; a CUSUM detector with parameters N, delta and tau decides.

papers.title: Playing it Safe: Adversarial Robustness with an Abstain Option

papers.method: Abstention objective; adversarially trained classifier abstaining near the decision boundary; CARL learns classifier and abstention region together; PGD and DeepFool variants.

papers.title: Beyond Confidence: Adaptive Abstention in Dual-Threshold Conformal Prediction for Autonomous System Perception
papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Omni-layer Intelligent Systems (COINS) 2025 (arXiv 2502.07255)
papers.key_idea: Combines a conformal threshold for valid prediction sets with a separate abstention threshold chosen by ROC analysis, so perception abstains more as environmental perturbation grows.
papers.method: Two thresholds on nonconformity scores: one for coverage, one for abstention picked to maximize TPR minus FPR on calibration data.

papers.title: Towards Streaming Perception
papers.key_idea: Introduces streaming accuracy, a metric scoring the perception output at every time instant so latency counts, and a meta-benchmark turning single-frame tasks into streaming tasks; finds an accuracy-latency sweet spot.
papers.method: Evaluates the output of the whole stack against the world state at each time instant; detection and instance segmentation on urban video; scheduling and forecasting baselines.

papers.title: StreamYOLO: Real-time Object Detection for Streaming Perception
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR) 2022 (arXiv 2207.10433)
papers.key_idea: Real-time detector that predicts the next frame from current and previous frame features (dual-flow module, trend-aware loss), improving streaming accuracy on Argoverse-HD.
papers.method: Dual Flow Perception fuses features of two adjacent frames; Trend Aware Loss weights objects by speed; mix-velocity training; velocity-aware streaming AP.

papers.title: LongShortNet: Exploring Temporal and Semantic Features Fusion in Streaming Perception
papers.key_idea: Dual-path streaming detector that fuses short-term spatial features with features of a few earlier frames kept in a buffer, adding almost no latency.
papers.method: ShortPath on the current frame, LongPath on stored features of N earlier frames, late fusion with dilation; N=3 chosen.

papers.title: DAMO-StreamNet: Optimizing Streaming Perception in Autonomous Driving
papers.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI) 2023 (arXiv 2303.17144)
papers.key_idea: Streaming detector adding a deformable-convolution neck, a dual-path short and long temporal branch, logits distillation and a real-time forecasting update; scores above StreamYOLO and LongShortNet.
papers.method: Dynamic receptive field neck; dual-path temporal fusion; teacher-student logits distillation; support-frame update during inference.

papers.title: BDD100K: A Diverse Driving Dataset for Heterogeneous Multitask Learning
papers.key_idea: Large open driving video dataset: 100,000 clips of 40 s with GPS and IMU, diverse in place, weather and time of day, with 10 tasks including multi-object tracking.

papers.title: PADetBench: Towards Benchmarking Physical Attacks against Object Detection
papers.key_idea: CARLA-based benchmark of 20 physical attack methods against 48 detectors under controlled weather, view and distance, with pipelines to generate aligned clean and attacked image datasets.

papers.key_idea: Releases Drive-By-Fly-By, a real-world video test set (44 scenarios) of traffic signs and vehicles with physical sticker triggers, including object-disappearance cases, and finds standard digital poisoning ineffective against detectors in the field.
