papers.key_idea: Malicious participants in collaborative perception send crafted data that cause hard brakes or collision risk; benign vehicles jointly reveal the fabrication with an anomaly detector built on agreement across their views.
papers.method: Real-time data fabrication attacks on shared perception data; systematic anomaly detection in which benign vehicles cross-check the shared perception jointly.

papers.title: Among Us: Adversarially Robust Collaborative Perception by Consensus
papers.venue: 2023 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
papers.key_idea: ROBOSAC: collaboration should agree with individual perception, so results with and without random subsets of teammates are compared until consensus, rejecting attackers without knowing the attack.
papers.method: Hypothesize-and-verify sampling over teammate subsets; analysis of how many trials guarantee an attacker-free subset of a given size, or the largest such subset within a trial budget.

papers.title: MADE: Malicious Agent Detection for Robust Multi-Agent Collaborative Perception
papers.venue: 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
papers.key_idea: Each agent tests every collaborator for consistency with its own view through two hypothesis tests and removes agents judged malicious, with the false-positive rate controlled by the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.
papers.method: Semi-supervised anomaly detector; double hypothesis test on a match-loss statistic and a collaborative reconstruction-loss statistic, both measuring ego-collaborator consistency.

papers.title: CP-Guard+: A New Paradigm for Malicious Agent Detection and Defense in Multi-Agent Collaborative Perception
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
papers.key_idea: Title only: detection of and defense against malicious agents in multi-agent collaborative perception, presented by the authors as a new paradigm.

papers.title: Understanding the Robustness of 3D Object Detection with Bird's-Eye-View Representations in Autonomous Driving
papers.key_idea: Benchmarks natural and adversarial robustness of multi-camera BEV 3D detectors and adds a patch attack placed in 3D space so that it stays consistent across views and time.
papers.method: Evaluation of BEV and non-BEV camera detectors and of BEV fusion under corruptions and adversarial noise; 3D-consistent patch attack.

papers.title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Camera-based 3D Object Detection
papers.key_idea: Studies leading camera-based 3D detectors under white-box and black-box, pixel and patch attacks on classification and localisation; finds that benign multi-frame input and accurate depth both improve robustness.
papers.method: Systematic attack evaluation across detector families (BEV, depth-estimation-based, depth-free), two attack settings, two objectives and two attack types.

papers.title: Protecting Autonomous Cars from Phantom Attacks
papers.key_idea: Journal article on protecting cars from phantom attacks; its one-sentence record abstract says it enables object detectors to better separate real from fake objects in semi-autonomous and fully autonomous vehicles.
papers.method: Not read in this run. The CCS 2020 paper by the same first author (row P2-P402 of LIT_A4) describes a committee of four small CNNs (light, context, surface, depth) that judges each detected object; whether this article presents the same countermeasure is UNVERIFIED.

papers.title: MobilBye: Attacking ADAS with Camera Spoofing
papers.key_idea: A drone-carried portable projector presents a spoofed traffic sign to a driving car and the Mobileye driver-assistance unit reads it as a real sign; colour, shape, projection speed, diameter and ambient light are varied.
papers.method: Physical experiment: spoofed signs injected into a Mobileye unit by projection while sign colour, shape, projection speed, diameter and ambient light are changed.

papers.title: bAdvertisement: Attacking Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems Using Print Advertisements
papers.venue: 2022 IEEE European Symposium on Security and Privacy Workshops (EuroS&PW)
papers.key_idea: Title-level: an attack on advanced driver-assistance systems delivered through print advertisements, a creation medium that needs no projector or screen (abstract not read).
papers.method: Not read.

papers.title: Seeing isn't Believing
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 2019 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security
papers.key_idea: Robust physical adversarial examples for detectors in two forms: a hiding attack and an appearing attack whose nested design joins two patterns so a false object is detected at long and short distance.
papers.method: Hiding: feature-interference reinforcement and enhanced realistic constraints generation. Appearing: nested adversarial example that combines two examples, made in varied styles to look less suspicious.

papers.title: Fooling the Eyes of Autonomous Vehicles: Robust Physical Adversarial Examples Against Traffic Sign Recognition Systems
papers.venue: Proceedings 2022 Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
papers.key_idea: Pipeline for physical adversarial examples against detector-based traffic sign recognition on streaming video, covering four attack vectors: hiding, appearance, non-target and target attacks.
papers.method: Image-transformation distribution extended with blur and resolution changes to imitate in-vehicle cameras; single and multiple bounding-box filters for efficient perturbation training.

papers.title: Rogue Signs: Deceiving Traffic Sign Recognition with Malicious Ads and Logos
papers.key_idea: Sign Embedding attack: innocuous signs and advertisements are modified so that a traffic sign recogniser classifies them as an attacker-chosen traffic sign with high confidence, so no existing sign needs to be touched.
papers.method: Adversarial optimisation over a set of image transformations; printed samples tested in drive-by runs at varied distance, lighting and camera angle, plus virtual tests.

papers.title: DARTS: Deceiving Autonomous Cars with Toxic Signs
papers.key_idea: Two ways to make toxic signs: out-of-distribution attacks that start from arbitrary images instead of real signs, and a lenticular printing attack that uses an optical effect to fool sign recognition.
papers.method: Out-of-distribution adversarial examples and lenticular printing; virtual and real-world tests under white-box and black-box threat models.

papers.title: Poltergeist: Acoustic Adversarial Machine Learning against Cameras and Computer Vision
papers.venue: 2021 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
papers.key_idea: Title-level: acoustic signals are used as an adversarial channel against cameras and computer vision (abstract not read). A later paper describes camera signal injection as adding image distortion (see notes).
papers.method: Not read.

papers.title: TPatch: A Triggered Physical Adversarial Patch
papers.key_idea: A printed patch stays benign until acoustic signal injection toward the camera adds a designed distortion; it then launches a hiding, creating or altering attack on detectors and classifiers, with content-based camouflage.
papers.method: Patch optimised to act only under the injected distortion; content-based camouflage against driver suspicion; robustness enhancement for the physical world.

papers.title: DoubleStar: Long-Range Attack Towards Depth Estimation based Obstacle Avoidance in Autonomous Systems
papers.key_idea: Light from two complementary sources exploits stereo matching and lens flare to inject fake obstacle depth into stereo cameras, so an obstacle-avoidance system reacts to an obstacle that is not there.
papers.method: Two attack formats, projected light beams and lens-flare orbs; tests on two commercial stereo cameras, an Ardupilot simulation and a commercial drone.

papers.title: TOG: Targeted Adversarial Objectness Gradient Attacks on Real-time Object Detection Systems
papers.key_idea: Three perturbation attacks on real-time detectors named by their effect: object-vanishing, object-fabrication and object-mislabeling, plus a universal variant that transfers to black-box models at negligible attack-time cost.
papers.method: Targeted objectness-gradient attacks on the detection network (the name of the method); a universal objectness-gradient variant uses adversarial transferability for black-box attacks on edge systems.

papers.title: Physically Realizable Adversarial Creating Attack Against Vision-Based BEV Space 3D Object Detection
papers.key_idea: Title-level: a physically realizable creating attack against vision-based bird-eye-view 3D object detection, the camera-only 3D detection setting of driving stacks (abstract not read).
papers.method: Not read.

papers.title: Daedalus: Breaking Nonmaximum Suppression in Object Detection via Adversarial Examples
papers.key_idea: Adversarial examples shrink detection boxes so that non-maximum suppression no longer merges them, leaving extremely dense false positives; an ensemble of substitute models gives black-box transfer, and printed posters carry the attack.
papers.method: Optimisation that compresses box dimensions to evade non-maximum suppression; ensemble of popular detection models as substitutes; poster demonstration.

papers.title: Phantom Sponges: Exploiting Non-Maximum Suppression to Attack Deep Object Detectors
papers.venue: 2023 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
papers.key_idea: A universal perturbation adds many phantom objects that overload non-maximum suppression and slow each frame, while the original objects stay detected so that the attack is noticed later.
papers.method: Universal adversarial perturbation aimed at the non-maximum suppression stage of the detection pipeline while preserving the original detections.

papers.title: TrackFlood: Relocating Latency Attacks from NMS-Free Detectors to Real-Time Trackers
papers.key_idea: For detectors without non-maximum suppression, perturbations flood the multi-object tracker with spatially spread phantom detections; a bounded-admission layer that caps tracker workload restores latency at a cost in admitted clean detections.
papers.method: White-box overload attack on detect-then-track pipelines with one-to-one and query-based detectors; a lightweight, architecture-agnostic admission cap is evaluated as the defence.

papers.title: Exploring the Vulnerability of Single Shot Module in Object Detectors via Imperceptible Background Patches
papers.key_idea: Small perturbations placed only in background patches, outside every object box, cut true positives and sharply raise false positives, because the effective receptive field of single-shot modules is larger than the object.
papers.method: Search for a few background patches and imperceptible perturbations on them, against region proposal networks and single-stage detectors.

papers.title: Detecting Adversarial Perturbations in Multi-Task Perception
papers.venue: 2022 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
papers.key_idea: Flags adversarial inputs when edges extracted from the image, the predicted depth and the predicted segmentation disagree; an edge-consistency training loss tightens the benign agreement first.
papers.method: Multi-task network (depth estimation and semantic segmentation); edge inconsistency score across the three modalities; a multi-task attack aimed at both tasks and at the detection scheme is also built.

papers.title: Connecting the Dots: Detecting Adversarial Perturbations Using Context Inconsistency
papers.key_idea: Learns context consistency rules during training and checks them at test time: one auto-encoder per object class outputs a discrepancy when a perturbation makes an object out of place in its scene.
papers.method: Detector augmented with class-specific auto-encoders over context information; the input-output discrepancy signals a violated context rule.

papers.title: Exorcising ''Wraith'': Protecting LiDAR-based Object Detector in Automated Driving System from Appearing Attacks
papers.key_idea: Plug-in module beside a LiDAR detector removes forged obstacles whose local parts score low objectness; the predictor uses the physical relation between depth and point density, which appearing attacks violate.
papers.method: Local objectness predictor with explicit depth input; obstacles with a major share of low-objectness parts are eliminated; closed-loop control driving tests in simulation with Baidu Apollo.

papers.title: Formalizing and evaluating requirements of perception systems for automated vehicles using spatio-temporal perception logic
papers.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research
papers.key_idea: Spatio-Temporal Perception Logic expresses requirements on perception output streams with spatial and temporal operators, allowing basic sanity checks of a perception system even without ground truth in some cases.
papers.method: Logic over perception data across frames; a fragment is monitorable offline in polynomial time; example specifications for vehicle perception systems.

papers.title: Too Afraid to Drive: Systematic Discovery of Semantic DoS Vulnerability in Autonomous Driving Planning under Physical-World Attacks
papers.venue: Proceedings 2022 Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
papers.key_idea: Treats overly conservative planning as a security problem: harmless-looking physical objects placed by an attacker, such as off-road cardboard boxes, cause failed or badly degraded missions; PlanFuzz finds such cases.
papers.method: Dynamic testing with planning invariants as test oracles, constrained input generation for attacker-placed objects and a vulnerability distance metric that guides the search.

papers.title: Does Physical Adversarial Example Really Matter to Autonomous Driving? Towards System-Level Effect of Adversarial Object Evasion Attack
papers.venue: 2023 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
papers.key_idea: Measurement study: published STOP-sign evasion attacks are evaluated in a full driving pipeline and none produces a system-level effect such as a traffic rule violation; a system-driven attack design (SysAdv) raises the violation rate.
papers.method: System-level evaluation with the full driving pipeline, a vehicle plant model and physically consistent object sizes; new attack design built on the two limitations found.

papers.title: Evaluating Adversarial Attacks on Driving Safety in Vision-Based Autonomous Vehicles
papers.key_idea: End-to-end evaluation framework with driving-safety metrics for perturbation and patch attacks on stereo 3D object detectors; the attack impact on detection precision and the impact on driving safety turn out to be decoupled.
papers.method: Evaluation of two vision-based 3D detectors under two attack types with a set of driving safety performance metrics; ablation study on the causes of the findings.

papers.title: Knowledge Enhanced Machine Learning Pipeline against Diverse Adversarial Attacks
papers.key_idea: Combines a main sign classifier with weak auxiliary models for sign shape and sign content through first-order logic rules in a probabilistic graphical model, so predictions that contradict this domain knowledge are corrected.
papers.method: Probabilistic graphical model over the main DNN and auxiliary models linked by first-order logic rules; convergence and robustness theory under stated conditions; road sign recognition as the worked example.

papers.title: Redesigning Traffic Signs to Mitigate Machine-Learning Patch Attacks
papers.key_idea: Treats the traffic-sign standard itself as the defense: pictograms and colours are optimised under constraints so that models trained on the redesigned signs resist patch attacks while people still recognise the signs.
papers.method: Framework with three inputs (a sign standard with modifiable features and constraints, an adversarial training method, a function that synthesises realistic sign images); it outputs an optimised standard; user study on human recognisability.

papers.title: A Hybrid Defense Method against Adversarial Attacks on Traffic Sign Classifiers in Autonomous Vehicles
papers.key_idea: Sign classifier hardened by three combined steps: random crop-and-resize filtering, plurality voting over an ensemble, and an optical character recognition model used as a local feature mapper.
papers.method: Transfer-learned Inception-V3 and ResNet-152 sign classifiers combined with random filtering, ensembling and OCR-based local feature mapping.

papers.title: BlurNet: Defense by Filtering the Feature Maps
papers.key_idea: Defense aimed at the RP2 stop-sign sticker attack: RP2 adds high-frequency noise visible in first-layer feature maps, so the network low-pass filters those maps or is trained with regularisers that produce this behaviour.
papers.method: Frequency analysis of first-layer feature maps; depthwise convolution layer of blur kernels after the first layer; regularisation schemes including total variation; black-box transfer, white-box and adaptive attack evaluation.

papers.title: Defending Against Physically Realizable Attacks on Image Classification
papers.key_idea: Finds that PGD adversarial training and randomized smoothing protect little against physically realizable attacks, then trains classifiers against an abstract rectangular occlusion attack to gain robustness to them.
papers.method: Rectangular occlusion attack model with two efficient ways to compute the adversarial rectangle; adversarial training with that attack.

papers.title: One Signature, Two Threats: Grammar Scored Cross-Channel Disagreement for Robust Traffic Sign Recognition
papers.key_idea: Treats both attacks and benign degradation as one observable signature: localized disagreement among independent shape, colour and pictogram cues, scored against a small grammar of valid attribute tuples, with per-channel abstention.
papers.method: SAFER-Sign: decorrelated shape, colour and glyph encoders; evidential per-channel uncertainty; soft factorized confidence-gated sign-grammar prior; spatial reliability gate anchored to a parameter-free cross-channel disagreement signal.

papers.title: Explainable and Trustworthy Traffic Sign Detection for Safe Autonomous Driving: An Inductive Logic Programming Approach
papers.venue: Electronic Proceedings in Theoretical Computer Science 385 (ICLP 2023)
papers.key_idea: Stop-sign recogniser that turns OpenCV colour masks, polygon shape and OCR text into logic facts and learns human-readable rules with inductive logic programming from very few examples.
papers.method: Background removal, colour masks, contour polygon fitting and EasyOCR text as predicates; Aleph and Metagol induce the rule; compared with a GTSRB-trained CNN.

papers.title: A survey of adversarial threats and defenses for traffic sign recognition in autonomous vehicles
papers.venue: International Journal of Cognitive Computing in Engineering
papers.key_idea: Traffic-sign-specific survey of attacks and defenses with a taxonomy by medium, objective, model access and phase; groups defenses into preprocessing, training, inference-time detection, verification and structure-aware reasoning over sign geometry, colour and semantics.
papers.method: Literature survey with a cognitive-computing framing; also covers TSR datasets, recognition pipelines, evaluation protocols and robustness metrics beyond attack success rate.

papers.title: PatchGuard-Freq: Zero-Overhead Adversarial Patch Defense via Frequency Detection and Data-Driven Robustness
papers.key_idea: Separates detection from mitigation for traffic-sign patch attacks: a frequency-domain detector flags attacked images, and adversarial fine-tuning restores the sign detector without adding any inference module.
papers.method: Frequency-domain analysis for patch detection; adversarial fine-tuning of the detector; defense-aware training against adaptive attacks.

papers.title: Research on Adversarial Patch Attack Defense Method for Traffic Sign Detection
papers.venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
papers.key_idea: Detector-level patch defense: RP2-derived patches simulate damaged or maliciously modified signs, and YOLOv2 gets extra attacked-sign classes plus adversarial training, so patched signs are still detected.
papers.method: IYOLO-TS: YOLOv2 with attacked classes added to the last layer; patches obtained by attacking the detector with RP2 and training on blank patches; adversarial training.

papers.title: Retroreflectivity-Based Traffic Sign Cybersecurity Synthetic Data and Defense Models
papers.key_idea: Labels signs safe or not safe by retroreflectivity relative to MUTCD minimum thresholds, generates synthetic data with a conditional GAN, and studies adversarial training and hybrid quantum-classical networks for this classifier.
papers.method: cGAN data synthesis; CNN and two hybrid quantum-classical networks; FGSM and PGD attacks with adversarial training; cross-dataset checks on LISA and GTSRB samples.

papers.title: Road-Sign Detection and Recognition Based on Support Vector Machines
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
papers.key_idea: Classical pipeline that encodes the sign standard: HSI colour segmentation, then shape classification where the segmentation colour limits which shapes are possible, then content recognition only among signs of that colour and shape.
papers.method: Fixed hue and saturation thresholds plus achromatic decomposition for white; distance-to-borders vectors into linear SVMs per colour for shape (octagon treated as circle at distance); Gaussian-kernel SVMs for content.

papers.title: Image-based retro-reflectivity measurement of traffic signs in day time
papers.key_idea: Measures sign retroreflectivity in daylight from a vehicle-mounted camera by simulating nighttime visibility: flash and no-flash images are processed so that only the controlled light source remains.
papers.method: Flash and no-flash image pair, camera response calibration, removal of ambient light, luminance and illuminance from pixel values, retroreflectivity per pixel.

papers.title: Multi-view traffic sign detection, recognition, and 3D localisation
papers.key_idea: Mobile-mapping pipeline: colour and shape criteria propose candidates per view, and detections from eight calibrated cameras are fused into 3D sign hypotheses chosen by Minimum Description Length with geometric and shape consistency.
papers.method: Colour- and shape-based candidate extraction, bounded AdaBoost evaluation, multi-view hypothesis generation with geometric and visual consistency, MDL pruning, SVM type voting across views.

papers.title: Traffic Sign Detection Under Challenging Conditions: A Deeper Look into Performance Variations and Spectral Characteristics
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
papers.key_idea: CURE-TSD-Real video benchmark with 12 simulated challenge types at 5 levels (rain, haze, shadow, exposure, dirty lens and others) to measure how benign conditions degrade sign detection and how this shows in spectra.
papers.method: Controlled degradations of 49 real sequences; two benchmark detectors; magnitude spectra of residual videos correlated with detection loss.

papers.title: Traffic Sign Classifiers Under Physical World Realistic Sticker Occlusions: A Cross Analysis Study
papers.key_idea: Studies realistic-looking stickers, both vandalism and optimised placement, on 11 sign classifiers; finds that covering the few distinctive features of a class, not salient adversarial texture, drives misclassification.
papers.method: Sticker content matched to brightness, contrast and blur; random, structured and model-cross (MCSA) placement; cross-model transfer analysis; dashboard field tests including RP2 and AP.

papers.title: Runtime Monitoring Neuron Activation Patterns
papers.venue: Design, Automation and Test in Europe Conference and Exhibition (DATE)
papers.key_idea: Replays the training data after training to store neuron activation patterns in abstract form; at run time a decision whose pattern is not within a Hamming-distance threshold of a stored pattern raises a warning.
papers.method: Activation-pattern abstraction of a monitored layer built from training data; Hamming-distance membership test per input; the threshold trades warnings against false positives.

papers.title: Outside the Box: Abstraction-Based Monitoring of Neural Networks
papers.venue: European Conference on Artificial Intelligence (ECAI 2020), Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications
papers.key_idea: Monitors hidden layers instead of output confidence: per neuron, boxes span the values seen in training, and an input whose activations fall outside the boxes is flagged as novel.
papers.method: Box abstraction (an interval per neuron, borrowed from program analysis) over monitored layers; tunable trade-off between false warnings and detected novel inputs.

papers.title: Into the Unknown: Active Monitoring of Neural Networks
papers.venue: Runtime Verification (RV 2021), Lecture Notes in Computer Science
papers.key_idea: A monitor running beside a classifier asks a human for labels through interpretable queries and adapts incrementally, so it can separate newly learned classes from still-unknown ones; an adaptive quantitative monitor improves precision.
papers.method: Active monitoring framework: labeling queries to a human user, incremental adaptation of classifier and monitor, adaptive quantitative monitor.

papers.title: Did You Miss the Sign? A False Negative Alarm System for Traffic Sign Detectors
papers.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
papers.key_idea: A separate false-negative detector reads internal features of a single-shot traffic-sign detector and raises an alarm when the detector has discarded a sign it should have reported.
papers.method: SSD traffic-sign detector; a second network trained on its internal features decides whether a sign was missed; the alarm is scored with precision and recall.

papers.title: Online Monitoring of Object Detection Performance During Deployment
papers.venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
papers.key_idea: A cascaded network reads the object detector's internal features and predicts the quality of its mean average precision over a sliding window of input frames, so silent performance drops during deployment become visible.
papers.method: Cascaded neural network on detector internal features; sliding-window mAP quality prediction; several detector and driving-dataset combinations.

papers.title: Monitoring of perception systems: Deterministic, probabilistic, and learning-based fault detection and identification
papers.key_idea: Formalises runtime fault detection and identification for perception systems, models diagnostic information as a diagnostic graph, and gives deterministic, probabilistic and learning-based algorithms with guarantees and fundamental limits.
papers.method: Diagnostic graph over perception modules; fault detection and identification algorithms; failure modes recreated in the LGSVL simulator and monitors applied to the Apollo Auto stack.

papers.title: Unifying Evaluation of Machine Learning Safety Monitors
papers.venue: IEEE International Symposium on Software Reliability Engineering (ISSRE)
papers.key_idea: Proposes three system-level metrics for runtime safety monitors: Safety Gain, Residual Hazard and Availability Cost, computed from return functions that state how each prediction affects future rewards and hazards.
papers.method: Formal metric definitions; three use cases (classification, drone landing, autonomous driving) show how metrics from the literature map onto them.

papers.title: Out-of-Distribution Detection Is Not All You Need
papers.key_idea: Argues that runtime monitors should be judged on discarding incorrect predictions (out-of-model-scope detection) rather than on spotting inputs unlike the training data; good OOD scores can give a false impression of safety.
papers.method: Conceptual comparison of the OOD and out-of-model-scope settings; experiments on common datasets; monitors trained after removing erroneous training samples.

papers.title: Runtime Monitoring for Out-of-Distribution Detection in Object Detection Neural Networks
papers.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (2023 conference proceedings)
papers.key_idea: Extends a runtime monitor designed for classification networks to object detectors that identify and localise several objects, and tests it on several kinds of out-of-distribution settings.
papers.method: Runtime-monitoring approach transferred from classifiers to multi-object detection; experimental analysis across OOD settings.

papers.title: SAFE: Sensitivity-Aware Features for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
papers.key_idea: Per-detection features from residual layers with batch normalisation separate in- from out-of-distribution detections; an MLP trained to tell adversarially perturbed from clean in-distribution samples serves as a surrogate needing no OOD data.
papers.method: Extract SAFE vectors for every detected object of a frozen detector; train a multilayer perceptron on clean versus adversarially perturbed examples; no retraining of the detector and no generative model.

papers.title: Out-of-Distribution Detection for Automotive Perception
papers.venue: IEEE International Intelligent Transportation Systems Conference (ITSC)
papers.key_idea: OOD detection for automotive object classification that needs no OOD training data and adds no inference cost, meant to trigger a safe fallback mode when inputs are not covered by training.
papers.method: Alternative to softmax-based confidence for OOD decisions (mechanism not detailed in the abstract); compared with state-of-the-art methods on real-world automotive datasets.

papers.title: Anomaly Detection in Autonomous Driving: A Survey
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
papers.key_idea: Surveys anomaly detection for automated driving on camera, lidar, radar, multimodal and object-level data, and systematises methods by detection approach, corner-case level and suitability for online use.
papers.method: Literature survey with a systematisation by detection approach, corner-case level, online applicability and further attributes; research gaps named.

papers.title: Provably-Robust Runtime Monitoring of Neuron Activation Patterns
papers.venue: Design, Automation and Test in Europe Conference and Exhibition (DATE)
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: makes activation-pattern runtime monitoring provably robust; what the robustness covers (for example bounded input perturbations) was not read.
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only).

papers.title: Misbehaviour prediction for autonomous driving systems
papers.venue: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Software Engineering (ICSE)
papers.key_idea: SelfOracle monitors a driving network at run time with autoencoder reconstruction and time-series anomaly detection to predict unsupported scenarios before misbehaviours such as leaving the road or colliding.
papers.method: Autoencoder reconstruction of driving scenes plus time-series anomaly detection sets a confidence boundary between normal and unsupported conditions; anomalous contexts injected in the Udacity simulator.

papers.title: A Simple Unified Framework for Detecting Out-of-Distribution Samples and Adversarial Attacks
papers.key_idea: Fits class-conditional Gaussians to low- and upper-level features of a pre-trained softmax classifier and scores inputs by Mahalanobis distance, detecting both out-of-distribution samples and adversarial attacks with one score.
papers.method: Gaussian discriminant analysis on intermediate features; Mahalanobis-distance confidence score; applies to any pre-trained softmax classifier.

papers.title: VOS: Learning What You Don't Know by Virtual Outlier Synthesis
papers.key_idea: Samples virtual outliers from low-likelihood regions of class-conditional feature distributions during training and adds an unknown-aware contrastive objective, so detectors separate in-distribution from out-of-distribution objects better.
papers.method: Feature-space outlier synthesis plus an unknown-aware training objective; evaluated on object detection and image classification models.

papers.title: Safety Concerns and Mitigation Approaches Regarding the Use of Deep Learning in Safety-Critical Perception Tasks
papers.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (2020 proceedings)
papers.key_idea: Enumerates technical safety concerns of deep learning in perception pipelines, discusses possible mitigation methods for each, and names the mitigations still missing for a safety argument.
papers.method: Structured enumeration of safety concerns with a discussion of mitigations and gaps.

papers.title: Deep Learning Safety Concerns in Automated Driving Perception
papers.key_idea: Refines the safety-concern concept for DNN perception in automated driving using expert feedback and an added categorisation; the concept aligns with ISO 21448 (SOTIF) and informed ISO PAS 8800.
papers.method: Concept paper: safety concerns as the structuring element, refined with domain and safety experts, plus a categorisation for cross-functional teams.

papers.title: Safety Monitoring of Machine Learning Perception Functions: A Survey
papers.key_idea: Reviews safety monitors for ML perception in safety-critical systems and structures their design into threat identification, requirements elicitation, failure detection, reaction and evaluation, with open challenges.
papers.method: Extensive literature review organised by five design factors; challenges and research directions.

papers.title: Run-Time Monitoring of Machine Learning for Robotic Perception: A Survey of Emerging Trends
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: survey of emerging trends in run-time monitoring of machine-learning perception on robots; abstract not read.
papers.method: Survey (not read).

papers.title: Introspection of DNN-Based Perception Functions in Automated Driving Systems: State-of-the-Art and Open Research Challenges
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: state of the art and open research challenges of introspection for DNN-based perception functions in automated driving; abstract not read.
papers.method: Survey (not read).

papers.title: Introspection of 2D Object Detection using Processed Neural Activation Patterns in Automated Driving Systems
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: introspection of a 2D object detector in automated driving from processed neural activation patterns; abstract not read.
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only); the title names processed neural activation patterns.

papers.title: Run-Time Introspection of 2D Object Detection in Automated Driving Systems Using Learning Representations
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: run-time introspection of 2D object detection in automated driving based on learned representations; abstract not read.

papers.title: Predicting Safety Misbehaviours in Autonomous Driving Systems Using Uncertainty Quantification
papers.venue: IEEE Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation (ICST)
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: uncertainty quantification used to predict safety misbehaviours of autonomous driving systems; abstract not read.
papers.method: Not read (metadata-only).

papers.title: ThirdEye: Attention Maps for Safe Autonomous Driving Systems
papers.venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE)
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: attention maps applied to the safety of autonomous driving systems; abstract not read.

papers.title: WIP: On Robustness of Lane Detection Models to Physical-World Adversarial Attacks
papers.venue: Proceedings Fourth International Workshop on Automotive and Autonomous Vehicle Security (AutoSec 2022, NDSS workshop)
papers.key_idea: Work-in-progress empirical study of how four major types of lane detection methods hold up under three physical-world adversarial attacks, among them the dirty road patch attack; robustness differs by method.
papers.method: Re-runs existing physical-world lane attacks (dirty road patch, drawn lane lines) against several lane-detector families and compares their security properties.

papers.title: Model-Agnostic Defense for Lane Detection against Adversarial Attack
papers.venue: Proceedings Third International Workshop on Automotive and Autonomous Vehicle Security (AutoSec 2021, NDSS workshop)
papers.key_idea: A defense for lane detection designed to work independently of the lane model it protects (title-level reading; abstract not read).

papers.title: Towards Driving-Oriented Metric for Lane Detection Models
papers.venue: 2022 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Proposes a driving-oriented metric for judging lane detection models (title-level reading; abstract not read).

papers.method: Prediction-consistency test under cheap input transformations, with joint detection over several squeezers.

papers.title: Local Gradients Smoothing: Defense Against Localized Adversarial Attacks
papers.venue: 2019 IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
papers.key_idea: Training-free patch defense: locate localized adversarial noise from concentrated high-frequency gradients and suppress those regions before inference, with little effect on the salient object.
papers.method: Gradient-domain localization of patch noise and regularization of image gradients in that region.

papers.method: Saliency-map localisation, guided feature transplantation with a label-consistency test, GAN inpainting for mitigation.

papers.title: Black-box Explanation of Object Detectors via Saliency Maps

papers.title: ODAM: Gradient-based instance-specific visual explanations for object detection

papers.method: Model randomization test scored with qualitative criteria and SSIM; guided backpropagation, integrated gradients and SmoothGrad variants; class and box explanations.

papers.title: DExT: Detector Explanation Toolkit
papers.key_idea: Toolkit that explains both box and class decisions of SSD512, Faster R-CNN and EfficientDet-D0 with gradient methods, merges multi-object explanations into one view, and ranks methods by insertion, deletion and a user study.
papers.method: Guided backpropagation, integrated gradients and SmoothGrad variants per decision; four multi-object visualisations (PCA, contours, density clustering, convex polygons); insertion and deletion in single-box and realistic settings; user study.

papers.title: G-CAME: Gaussian-Class Activation Mapping Explainer for Object Detectors

papers.method: Class activation mapping combined with a Gaussian kernel (title and benchmark description); per-detection saliency.

papers.venue: Proceedings of the Workshop of the Austrian Association for Pattern Recognition (OAGM 2021)
papers.key_idea: Integrates Grad-CAM into YOLO by tracing each kept box back through non-maximum suppression to its objectness and class neurons, giving per-detection attribution maps; normalization strongly changes how maps read.
papers.method: Grad-CAM on the last convolutional layer of the YOLO head for the neurons behind a chosen detection; detection-, image- and dataset-level normalization compared.

papers.title: Fast Explanation Using Shapley Value for Object Detection
papers.key_idea: Trains an explainer network to estimate per-pixel Shapley values for every detected object, so detector saliency maps are produced in real time at test time without sampling.
papers.method: Learned explainer model approximating Shapley values per object (abstract fragment and survey description).

papers.title: Rethinking explainable AI: The gap between saliency-based explanation and user understanding for object detection models
papers.key_idea: User study with tasks that measure understanding of an object detector at feature, instance and system level; showing the detector output helped, while adding saliency maps gave no further benefit.
papers.method: Forward and counterfactual simulation tasks before and after training with or without saliency explanations; eye-movement analysis.

papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI 2020)
papers.key_idea: Adversarial examples spread their feature attributions differently from clean inputs; thresholding a dispersion statistic of leave-one-out attribution maps, extended across layers, flags them.

papers.title: When Explainability Meets Adversarial Learning: Detecting Adversarial Examples using SHAP Signatures
papers.key_idea: Uses SHAP values computed for internal layers of the protected network as a signature of each input and trains a separate classifier on these signatures to tell adversarial from benign inputs.
papers.method: SHAP explanation signatures from hidden layers fed to a binary detector (description in citing papers).

papers.title: NeuroShield: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Adversarial Robustness
papers.key_idea: Adds symbolic attribute heads (shape, colour, icon, category) to a traffic sign classifier and trains with semantic and logic losses that enforce class-implies-attribute rules, aiming at robustness and interpretable predictions.
papers.method: Modified ResNet18 with shared features for class and attribute heads; soft implication rules from class-wise attribute dictionaries; adversarial training with FGSM or PGD.

papers.title: Fooling Network Interpretation in Image Classification
papers.venue: 2019 IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
papers.key_idea: Adversarial patches optimized to cause misclassification while suppressing Grad-CAM at the patch, so the interpretation no longer reveals the attack; doubles as a controlled test of interpretation reliability.
papers.method: Patch optimization with an added loss on the Grad-CAM heat map at the patch location; transfer to occluding-patch interpretation tested.

papers.title: SoK: Explainable Machine Learning in Adversarial Environments
papers.venue: 2024 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
papers.key_idea: Systematizes attacks on post-hoc explanation methods, defines a hierarchy of explanation-aware robustness notions, relates existing defenses to it and lists research gaps for explanations that resist manipulation.
papers.method: Systematization of knowledge: threat models, attack scopes and types, robustness notions, defense taxonomy.

papers.title: Are explainable AI (XAI) evaluation strategies aligned? Comparing subjective, objective, and mathematical evaluation measures using saliency maps
papers.key_idea: Preregistered user study comparing three saliency methods under subjective, objective and mathematical evaluation; the three families disagree, and mathematical metrics are not reliable proxies for user performance.
papers.method: Between-subjects study with trust and satisfaction questionnaires, accuracy-estimation and prediction tasks, and fidelity, complexity, robustness and localization metrics.

papers.title: ODExAI: A Comprehensive Object Detection Explainable AI Evaluation
papers.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science (book chapter)
papers.key_idea: Evaluation framework that scores detector explanation methods on faithfulness, localization and complexity, including run time, so method choice can follow the task.
papers.method: Quantitative metrics such as insertion, deletion, pointing game, energy-based pointing game and sparsity, plus run time, applied to several detector XAI methods.

papers.title: BSED: Baseline Shapley-Based Explainable Detector
papers.key_idea: Extends Baseline Shapley values to object detection so detector explanations satisfy the explainability axioms, with an approximation that keeps cost reasonable; model-agnostic, and explanations are used to correct detections.
papers.method: Baseline Shapley attribution per detection target with a cost-reducing approximation; compared on energy-based pointing game, deletion, insertion and axiom metrics.

papers.title: Human attention guided explainable artificial intelligence for computer vision models
papers.key_idea: Uses human attention maps as an objective plausibility measure for detector explanations and learns to combine gradient and activation maps to match human attention, raising plausibility, faithfulness and trust for detectors.
papers.method: FullGrad-CAM and FullGrad-CAM++ for object detection; HAG-XAI learns activation functions and smoothing kernels against human attention maps.

papers.title: WIP: From Detection to Explanation: Using LLMs for Adversarial Scenario Analysis in Vehicles
papers.venue: 3rd USENIX Symposium on Vehicle Security and Privacy (VehicleSec 2025)
papers.key_idea: Work in progress: structured scene descriptions plus the MUTCD traffic-control manual feed zero-shot chain-of-thought prompts so an LLM states whether an anomaly is a benign sensor error or an adversarial manipulation, and why.
papers.method: Domain-specific language encoding of vehicle and scene data; MUTCD as knowledge base; zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting; explanations compared with references by ROUGE, BLEU and SBERT plus manual review.

papers.title: Explanations Help: Leveraging Human Capabilities to Detect Cyberattacks on Automated Vehicles
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI 2025)
papers.key_idea: Online video study of whether in-vehicle displays help people detect attacks on infrastructure, perception and execution modules; alerts with explanations helped and softened false alarms, while bare alerts did worse than no display.
papers.method: Online video survey comparing no display, Alert and Alert plus Explanations across three attack types and alert-attack alignment conditions; detection, trust, situation awareness and usability measured.

papers.title: ARES: Adaptive robust object detection framework for enhancing real-time performance in autonomous vehicle systems
papers.key_idea: Run a fast low-security detector by default and switch to a costly certifiably robust detector only after a patch detector flags an attack, with schedulability analysis so detection tasks keep their deadlines.
papers.method: Mixed-criticality style mode switch triggered by a patch detector, plus fixed-priority schedulability analysis and priority assignment for multi-camera detection tasks.

papers.title: LanCeX: A Versatile and Lightweight Defense Method against Condensed Adversarial Attacks in Image and Audio Recognition
papers.venue: ACM Transactions on Embedded Computing Systems
papers.key_idea: Condensed (patch-like) perturbations cause abnormal activations that overwhelm semantic patterns; inference-inconsistency metrics flag such inputs at about one inference cost, followed by mitigation, aimed at embedded recognition.
papers.method: Activation-inconsistency metrics inside the CNN for detection, then data recovery; applied to image classification, object detection and audio recognition.

papers.title: Impact of Low-Bitwidth Quantization on the Adversarial Robustness for Embedded Neural Networks
papers.key_idea: Low-bitwidth quantization is not a reliable defense: apparent robustness comes from gradient masking, while adversarial examples transfer poorly between full-precision and quantized models.
papers.method: Evaluate binarized and low-bit quantized CNNs under gradient-based and gradient-free attacks and across bit-widths; explain poor transfer; sketch an ensemble defense.

papers.title: Evaluating the Impact of Adversarial Patch Attacks on YOLO Models and the Implications for Edge AI Security
papers.key_idea: Naturalistic adversarial patches regenerated for recent Ultralytics YOLO versions evade person detection; smaller models chosen for edge latency were less robust than larger ones.
papers.method: Port a naturalistic patch generator to YOLOv5, v8, v9 and v10; measure evasion; time inference on edge AI devices.

papers.title: RobustMQ: benchmarking robustness of quantized models
papers.key_idea: Benchmark of quantized ImageNet models under adversarial attacks, natural corruptions and systematic noise: quantized models resist attacks better but suffer more from corruptions and processing noise.
papers.method: Systematic robustness evaluation of quantized versus floating-point models across bit-widths and noise types.

papers.title: Segment and Recover: Defending Object Detectors Against Adversarial Patch Attacks
papers.key_idea: Training-free, patch-agnostic defense: localize large adversarial patches with an objectness-based frontend, then restore covered pixels by inpainting; reports a per-component runtime split.
papers.method: Patch localization frontend plus LaMa inpainting backend in front of unchanged detectors (YOLOv11, Faster R-CNN, DETR).

papers.title: Spear: Evaluate the Adversarial Robustness of Compressed Neural Models
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Third International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-24)
papers.key_idea: Attacks that maximise the behaviour gap between a compressed model and its dense reference expose extra risk from sparsity and quantization, on classification and object detection.
papers.method: Minimal-perturbation attack maximizing compressed-versus-dense output difference; tested on pruned (fine-grained, sparse tensor core) and INT8 QAT models.

papers.title: Can’t Slow Me Down: Learning Robust and Hardware-Adaptive Object Detectors against Latency Attacks for Edge Devices
papers.venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Latency attacks flood non-maximum suppression with phantom candidate boxes; background-attentive adversarial training tied to measured GPU capacity restores real-time detection on edge GPUs.
papers.method: Profile NMS cost against GPU capacity, use objectness loss as a proxy, add background attention to adversarial training; YOLOv3, v5 and v8 on Jetson Xavier NX, Jetson Orin NX, RTX 4070 Ti Super and A100.

papers.title: Time-Constrained Adversarial Defense in IoT Edge Devices through Kernel Tensor Decomposition and Multi-DNN Scheduling
papers.key_idea: eDenoizer lowers the latency of an adversarial denoiser on an edge device by Tucker-decomposing its convolution kernels and co-scheduling denoiser and protected model on a shared embedded GPU.
papers.method: Tensor decomposition of denoiser kernels plus priority-aware multi-DNN scheduling that projects CPU-side priorities onto a priority-agnostic GPU.

papers.title: RobustEdge: Low Power Adversarial Detection for Cloud-Edge Systems
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computational Intelligence
papers.key_idea: A reduced-precision detector with early detection and exit runs on the edge device and blocks adversarial inputs before they reach the cloud classifier, saving transmission and detection energy.
papers.method: Quantization-enabled energy separation training of 16-bit and 12-bit detectors; hardware evaluation on a 45 nm CMOS accelerator; Raspberry Pi energy comparison.

papers.title: WIP: A First Look At Employing Large Multimodal Models Against Autonomous Vehicle Attacks
papers.venue: Proceedings Symposium on Vehicle Security & Privacy (VehicleSec 2024)
papers.key_idea: A large multimodal model serves as a verification layer for traffic signs and is activated only when the vehicle is within about 7 m of a detected sign, to judge whether the sign is adversarial.
papers.method: Continuous sign detection and classification; GPT-4V queried on frames near the sign; tests with a stereo camera viewing attack images shown on a TV screen.

papers.title: Attention-Based Real-Time Defenses for Physical Adversarial Attacks in Vision Applications
papers.venue: 2024 ACM/IEEE 15th International Conference on Cyber-Physical Systems (ICCPS)
papers.key_idea: Physical adversarial objects over-activate a few channels in shallow layers; tracing those channels across video frames lets a defense detect and mask attacks with one inference pass per frame instead of two.
papers.method: Adversarial-Channel Attention Tracing (ACAT): a single-frame defense initializes the attack mask; channel attention on shallow layers then tracks the adversarial trace frame by frame.

papers.title: Model Agnostic Defense against Adversarial Patch Attacks on Object Detection in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
papers.venue: 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
papers.key_idea: A tiny single-stage model of about 1.2 million parameters handles adversarial patches in front of an unchanged UAV object detector and is sized for onboard deployment.
papers.method: Train a small patch-handling model on VisDrone; compare with segmentation-based patch masking; digital and physical tests; measure added processing time.

papers.title: Defending Person Detection Against Adversarial Patch Attack by Using Universal Defensive Frame
papers.key_idea: A universal defensive frame, optimized in competition with adversarial patches, is attached around the input image to protect person detection at very small added computation.
papers.method: Iterative competing optimization of patch and defensive frame; the frame is applied at inference in front of YOLO-v2 and Faster R-CNN.

papers.title: Noise Sensitivity-Based Energy Efficient and Robust Adversary Detection in Neural Networks
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
papers.key_idea: A layer-wise adversarial noise sensitivity metric picks where to attach a small binary detector; the quantized network plus detector stops adversarial inputs early and is priced in energy on scalable hardware.
papers.method: Noise-sensitivity layer selection, small neural detector, quantization of weights and activations, MAC and memory-access energy analysis with early exit.

papers.title: Relationship between Model Compression and Adversarial Robustness: A Review of Current Evidence
papers.venue: 2023 IEEE Symposium Series on Computational Intelligence (SSCI)
papers.key_idea: Review of studies on quantization, pruning and adversarial robustness: naive compression can reduce robustness, moderate pruning can preserve it, and past a critical compression ratio robustness falls before accuracy.
papers.method: Literature review comparing reported experiments on quantization, pruning and adversarial training.

papers.title: Quantization Robustness to Input Degradations for Object Detection
papers.venue: 2025 Innovations in Intelligent Systems and Applications Conference (ASYU)
papers.key_idea: Post-training quantization of YOLO detectors (FP32, FP16, dynamic UINT8, static INT8) tested under noise, blur, low contrast and JPEG degradations, with a degradation-aware INT8 calibration.
papers.method: Five YOLO12 scales converted with TensorRT and ONNX Runtime; COCO val2017 with synthetic degradations; RTX 2070 GPU.

papers.title: Robustness in Compressed Neural Networks for Object Detection
papers.venue: 2021 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
papers.key_idea: Pruned object detectors on autonomous-driving data: clean accuracy hides the cost of compression; sensitivity to synthetic distortions varies strongly by distortion type, and some classes lose far more than others.
papers.method: Structured and unstructured pruning of detectors; texture-invariant augmentation; tests under synthetic distortions and per-class accuracy; class-balancing remedies.

papers.title: Defensive Quantization: When Efficiency Meets Robustness
papers.key_idea: Conventional quantization keeps clean accuracy but loses much more accuracy under adversarial attack than full precision; a quantization method designed jointly for efficiency and robustness is proposed.
papers.method: Empirical study of quantized VGG-16 and Wide ResNet under FGSM on CIFAR-10, then a robustness-aware quantization scheme.

papers.title: Towards Building Self-Aware Object Detectors via Reliable Uncertainty Quantification and Calibration
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Self-aware object detection task: a detector must accept or reject a whole image from image-level uncertainty, give detection confidences calibrated for both classification and localisation (LaECE), and stay robust to domain shift.
papers.method: Image-level uncertainty from the most confident detections, reject threshold set with a pseudo-OOD set; per-class post-hoc calibrators; Detection Awareness Quality (DAQ) joins accuracy, calibration and image rejection.

papers.title: On Calibration of Object Detectors: Pitfalls, Evaluation and Baselines
papers.venue: European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV 2024), LNCS 15079
papers.key_idea: Shows that common detector calibration evaluation (D-ECE with AP, temperature scaling) misleads; proposes joint evaluation with LaECE0, LaACE0 and LRP at tuned thresholds, plus post-hoc Platt scaling and isotonic regression for detectors.
papers.method: Per-class thresholds cross-validated with LRP, then per-class post-hoc calibrators fitted on a held-out validation set; calibration errors align confidence with IoU to the matched ground truth.

papers.title: Deep neural rejection against adversarial examples
papers.key_idea: Rejects inputs whose feature representations look anomalous at several network layers, detecting adversarial examples without adversarial training, and evaluates against an adaptive white-box attack aware of the rejection.
papers.method: Reject option on a deep classifier using anomaly scores of representations at several layers; defense-aware adaptive white-box attack for evaluation.

papers.title: On optimum recognition error and reject tradeoff
papers.key_idea: Classic analysis of the optimum trade-off between recognition error and reject rate for a recognizer allowed to reject (title-level reading).
papers.method: Theory of the error-reject trade-off; text not read in this run.

papers.title: Sequential Tests of Statistical Hypotheses
papers.key_idea: Foundational paper on sequential tests of statistical hypotheses, in which the number of observations is not fixed in advance (title-level reading).
papers.method: Sequential hypothesis-testing theory; text not read in this run.

papers.title: Testing for outliers with conformal p-values
papers.key_idea: Builds conformal p-values for outlier detection that allow false discovery rate control, plus training-conditional p-values and a uniform confidence bound on the false positive rate of any outlier detector across thresholds.
papers.method: Conformal p-values computed against a clean reference set; multiple-testing control of false discoveries; concentration inequalities for training-conditional validity.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction: A Gentle Introduction
papers.venue: Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning
papers.key_idea: Hands-on introduction to conformal prediction and distribution-free uncertainty quantification for any pre-trained model, with extensions to structured outputs, distribution shift, time series, outliers and models that abstain.
papers.method: Tutorial with theory, worked examples and Python notebooks.

papers.title: Real-time Out-of-distribution Detection in Learning-Enabled Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.venue: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Cyber-Physical Systems (ICCPS)
papers.key_idea: Inductive conformal anomaly detection with nonconformity scores from a variational autoencoder or deep SVDD gives a real-time out-of-distribution monitor whose false alarm rate is well calibrated.
papers.method: Calibration split of the training data gives conformal p-values; an input is flagged when its p-value falls below a chosen significance level (paper text); VAE and deep SVDD as learned nonconformity measures.

papers.title: CODiT: Conformal Out-of-Distribution Detection in Time-Series Data for Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.venue: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Cyber-Physical Systems (ICCPS 2023)
papers.key_idea: Uses deviation from in-distribution temporal equivariance as the nonconformity score, combines several conformal detectors with Fisher's method, and flags out-of-distribution windows of consecutive inputs with bounded false alarms.
papers.method: Conformal anomaly detection on fixed-length windows of consecutive inputs; nonconformity from violated temporal equivariance; Fisher combination of independent conformal p-values.

papers.title: A Review and Comparative Study on Probabilistic Object Detection in Autonomous Driving
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
papers.key_idea: Reviews uncertainty estimation for deep object detection in driving, surveys probabilistic detectors and their evaluation metrics, and compares methods on one image detector across three public driving datasets.
papers.method: Survey plus a controlled comparative study built on a single image detector.

papers.title: Assurance monitoring of learning-enabled cyber-physical systems using inductive conformal prediction based on distance learning
papers.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing (AI EDAM)
papers.key_idea: Conformal prediction on learned low-dimensional embeddings gives each input a calibrated confidence; inputs whose prediction set holds more than one class are flagged for intervention, keeping a bounded error rate with few alarms.
papers.method: Distance learning to embed inputs; inductive conformal prediction at a chosen significance level; prediction sets with several classes are treated as a rejection that needs human intervention (publisher text extract).

papers.title: Systematic Evaluation of Uncertainty Calibration in Pretrained Object Detectors
papers.key_idea: Fair, repeatable framework for evaluating calibration of pretrained detectors of several paradigms under distributional shift and on out-of-distribution data; analyses why poor calibration emerges and improves it by fine-tuning only the last layer.
papers.method: Evaluation with proper scoring rules, calibration plots and errors, and entropy for spotting distributional change; comparison of detector paradigms, post-processing steps and metric choices (paper text extract).

papers.title: Three-way decisions with probabilistic rough sets
papers.key_idea: Theory of three-way decisions built on probabilistic rough sets (title-level reading).
papers.method: Decision theory with probabilistic rough sets; text not read in this run.

papers.title: Multivariate Confidence Calibration for Object Detection
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
papers.key_idea: Calibrates detector confidence jointly with box position and scale from the regression branch and introduces the detection expected calibration error (D-ECE), showing miscalibration depends on object location.
papers.method: Box-sensitive (multivariate) post-hoc calibration in a black-box setting with precision as the accuracy surrogate; D-ECE binned over confidence and box properties.

papers.title: Bridging Precision and Confidence: A Train-Time Loss for Calibrating Object Detection
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Auxiliary train-time loss that aligns the class confidence of boxes with their precision, through a differentiable proxy of minibatch true and false positive counts, to reduce calibration error in and out of domain.
papers.method: BPC loss added to the detector training loss; evaluated with D-ECE on in-domain and out-of-domain splits.

papers.title: Two Coupled Rejection Metrics Can Tell Adversarial Examples Apart
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Adds a reject option to adversarially trained classifiers: confidence and a learned rectified confidence (R-Con) form two coupled rejection metrics that provably separate correctly from wrongly classified inputs.
papers.method: Rectified rejection head sharing the backbone, trained with binary cross-entropy to predict true-label confidence; evaluated by accuracy at a fixed true positive rate and ROC-AUC, including adaptive attacks.

papers.title: Object Detection with Probabilistic Guarantees: A Conformal Prediction Approach
papers.key_idea: Applies split conformal prediction to object localization so predicted boxes come with probabilistic coverage guarantees, illustrated on pedestrian detection, and discusses theoretical and practical implications.
papers.method: Split conformal prediction on box-coordinate residuals from a calibration set; the guarantee holds on average over calibration sets under exchangeability (publisher page footnotes).

papers.title: Adaptive Bounding Box Uncertainties via Two-Step Conformal Prediction
papers.venue: European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV 2024), LNCS 15146
papers.key_idea: Two-step conformal procedure for multi-object detection: a conformal class-label set first, then box intervals that carry the label uncertainty, so coverage also holds for misclassified objects; ensemble and quantile variants adapt to object size.
papers.method: Class-conditional split conformal prediction for labels, then for box coordinates (Box-Std, Box-Ens, Box-CQR), on pretrained black-box detectors.

papers.title: Verifiably robust conformal prediction for probabilistic guarantees under adversarial attacks
papers.key_idea: Combines conformal prediction with neural network verification so prediction sets keep their coverage guarantee under norm-bounded adversarial perturbations, for classification and regression.
papers.method: VRCP: verification bounds applied at calibration time (VRCP-C) or at inference time (VRCP-I); compared with randomised-smoothing robust conformal methods.

papers.title: Unknown-Aware Object Detection: Learning What You Don't Know from Videos in the Wild
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Distils unknown object proposals from unlabeled video frames and regularises the detector with an energy-based uncertainty loss, so it can flag out-of-distribution objects instead of predicting them overconfidently.
papers.method: Spatial-temporal unknown distillation (STUD): unknown candidates found per frame and aggregated across frames; energy-based contrastive regularisation.

papers.title: The Overlooked Elephant of Object Detection: Open Set
papers.venue: IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
papers.key_idea: Formalises open-set object detection: unknown objects are often detected as known classes with very high confidence; proposes an open-set evaluation protocol and a metric (wilderness impact) for how unknowns degrade precision.
papers.method: Open-set protocol with detectors trained on PASCAL VOC and tested with unknown objects; precision under growing shares of unknown samples.

papers.title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017)
papers.key_idea: Builds a selective classifier on a trained network that rejects inputs as needed to guarantee a user-chosen risk with high probability while maximising coverage; frames performance as a risk-coverage curve.
papers.method: Selection with guaranteed risk: a threshold on a confidence-rate function (softmax response or MC-dropout) chosen with a high-probability bound on selective risk.

papers.title: Deep k-Nearest Neighbors: Towards Confident, Interpretable and Robust Deep Learning
papers.key_idea: Compares a test input with its nearest training neighbours in every layer's representation; conformal prediction on neighbour labels gives a credibility score that drops for adversarial or out-of-manifold inputs, and neighbours serve as explanations.
papers.method: Nearest-neighbour search in each layer; nonconformity from neighbour labels that disagree with the prediction; a held-out calibration set turns it into credibility.

papers.title: Benchmarking Robustness in Object Detection: Autonomous Driving when Winter is Coming
papers.key_idea: Benchmark of object detectors when image quality degrades: corrupted copies of Pascal VOC, COCO and Cityscapes with many corruption types; training on stylized images is offered as a simple robustness fix.
papers.method: Pascal-C, Coco-C and Cityscapes-C built by corrupting the images at several severities; standard detectors evaluated; stylized-image data augmentation tested.

papers.title: Rain Rendering for Evaluating and Improving Robustness to Bad Weather
papers.key_idea: Physics-based, data-driven and combined rain rendering adds controlled amounts of rain to existing driving datasets, so the loss of detection, segmentation and depth accuracy can be measured as rain increases.
papers.method: Particle simulator with rain photometric modelling, a data-driven variant and a combination of both; user study of realism; evaluation and finetuning of detection, segmentation and depth networks.

papers.title: Getting to know low-light images with the Exclusively Dark dataset
papers.key_idea: Exclusively low-light image set covering ten illumination types with image- and object-level labels; feature analysis indicates that low light alters detector features more deeply than simple illumination invariance can repair.
papers.method: Collection of visible-light low-light images; visual analysis of hand-crafted and learned features for object detection in low light.

papers.title: Traffic Sign Detection and Quality Assessment Using YOLOv8 in Daytime and Nighttime Conditions
papers.key_idea: YOLOv8 sign detection is evaluated by day and by night on a 16,500-image set, and detection is related to measured sign retroreflectivity, sharpness, brightness and contrast.
papers.method: YOLOv8 trained and tested on the ZND dataset; handheld retroreflectometer measurements of signs; video analysis of sharpness, brightness and contrast; human visibility ratings.

papers.title: RDPA: A concealed and perilous physical adversarial attack for nighttime traffic signs recognition
papers.key_idea: A low-reflectivity mask on a retroreflective sign blends in by day; under headlights at night it produces a light-dark contrast that drives a black-box targeted misclassification.
papers.method: Black-box reflectivity-difference attack; mask shape modelled with connected circles to form an irregular dark area; digital tests, then physical tests indoors and on roads.

papers.title: Benchmarking the Physical-world Adversarial Robustness of Vehicle Detection
papers.key_idea: CARLA-based data generation pipeline and the DCI dataset for comparing physical adversarial attacks on vehicle detectors across scenes, angles, distances, positions and weather.
papers.method: Simulated data generation in CARLA; three detection models and three physical adversarial attacks evaluated.

papers.title: ALLUDE: A Unified Evaluation System for Configurable Attacks in Differentiable Environments
papers.key_idea: Open-source system joining simulation and differentiable rendering to evaluate and optimise physical attacks on object detectors across scenes, objects, weather, lighting and camera trajectories.
papers.method: Latin Hypercube Sampling over 5,400 configurations (10 scene-object pairs, 9 weather conditions, 4 optimizers, 5 camera trajectories, 3 detection models); stress test of the CAMOU, RAUCA and FCA attacks.

papers.title: RAUCA: A Novel Physical Adversarial Attack on Vehicle Detectors via Robust and Accurate Camouflage Generation
papers.key_idea: Vehicle camouflage optimised through a neural renderer that models lighting and weather, with a multi-weather dataset in the loop so the attack holds across weather conditions.
papers.method: Neural Renderer Plus projects vehicle textures and renders environmental characteristics such as lighting and weather; multi-weather dataset used during camouflage generation.

papers.title: AdvRain: Adversarial Raindrops to Attack Camera-based Smart Vision Systems
papers.key_idea: A translucent sticker printed with raindrop-like blobs is placed over the camera lens; drop positions are found by random search so the blur misleads classifiers for all objects of a class.
papers.method: Iterative random search for critical drop positions; each drop is modelled as a blur of the image area it covers.

papers.title: Adversarial Rain Attack and Defensive Deraining for DNN Perception
papers.key_idea: Rain streaks are synthesised with learnable rain factors under a camera-exposure model and optimised to fool classifiers and object detectors; the same adversarial rain is used to harden deraining models.
papers.method: Factor-aware rain generation following the camera exposure process; adversarial rain augmentation with mixed rain layers for defensive deraining.

papers.title: Distracting Downpour: Adversarial Weather Attacks for Motion Estimation
papers.venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
papers.key_idea: Adversarially optimised particles that mimic snowflakes, rain streaks or fog clouds are rendered consistently over time and in 3D space to corrupt optical-flow estimation.
papers.method: Differentiable particle rendering over multiple time steps in 3D with photo-realistic appearance; particle optimisation against optical-flow networks; weather augmentation tested as a remedy.

papers.title: Learning to Enhance Low-Light Image via Zero-Reference Deep Curve Estimation
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
papers.key_idea: Low-light enhancement as per-image curve estimation by a small network trained without paired or unpaired reference images; the Zero-DCE++ variant has about 10K parameters.
papers.method: DCE-Net predicts pixel-wise high-order curves for dynamic-range adjustment; non-reference losses; an accelerated light version (Zero-DCE++).

papers.title: Image-Adaptive YOLO for Object Detection in Adverse Weather Conditions
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.key_idea: A small CNN predicts per-image parameters of a differentiable image-processing module; trained end to end with YOLOv3, the enhancement is tuned for detection in fog and low light, not for appearance.
papers.method: CNN-PP predicts the parameters of the DIP module; CNN-PP and YOLOv3 are learned jointly end to end in a weakly supervised way; one model handles normal and adverse-weather images.

papers.title: Bridging Day and Night: Target-Class Hallucination Suppression in Unpaired Image Translation
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.key_idea: Unpaired day-to-night translation tends to invent target-class objects such as traffic signs, vehicles and light effects; a segmenting discriminator finds these hallucinations and class prototypes push them out during translation.
papers.method: Dual-head discriminator that also performs semantic segmentation to find hallucinated content in background regions; class prototypes built from annotated target-domain objects act as anchors; iterative refinement on a Schroedinger-bridge translation model.

papers.title: Does Low-Light Image Enhancement Improve Object Detection? A Detection-Oriented and Cost-Aware Study on ExDark
papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Signal and Image Processing Applications (ICSIPA)
papers.key_idea: Title-level reading only: a study on ExDark of whether low-light image enhancement improves object detection, judged from the detection side and with computational cost in view; findings not read.

papers.title: FOLD: Low-Level Image Enhancement for Low-Light Object Detection Based on FPGA MPSoC
papers.key_idea: Low-order image enhancement expands the low-light training data of a YOLOv3 detector, which is then deployed on an FPGA system-on-chip board for efficient low-light detection at the edge.
papers.method: Low-order enhancement used to expand the low-light training data; YOLOv3 trained on it; deployment on a ZU3EG MPSoC board.
