papers.method: Guideline paper: methodological foundations, review of commonly accepted best practices and newly suggested evaluation methods; no experiment is named in the abstract.

papers.title: On Adaptive Attacks to Adversarial Example Defenses
papers.key_idea: Thirteen defenses from ICLR, ICML and NeurIPS that had reported adaptive evaluations are still circumvented; the paper teaches the methodology of building an adaptive attack instead of only reporting the broken result.
papers.method: Case studies: each defense is analysed and then attacked with an attack designed for that defense; the focus is on the approach, not on the end result.

papers.title: Obfuscated Gradients Give a False Sense of Security: Circumventing Defenses to Adversarial Examples
papers.key_idea: Gradient masking (obfuscated gradients) makes iterative optimization attacks fail without making a defense secure; three types are identified, each with an attack technique that overcomes it.
papers.method: Describes characteristic behaviours of defenses that obfuscate gradients; develops one attack technique per type; case study on the non-certified white-box-secure defenses of ICLR 2018.

papers.title: Reliable evaluation of adversarial robustness with an ensemble of diverse parameter-free attacks
papers.key_idea: Two parameter-free extensions of the PGD attack fix step-size and objective failures; with two existing attacks they form a user-independent ensemble that lowered the reported robust accuracy of almost every re-tested defense.
papers.method: Two PGD extensions combined with two complementary existing attacks into a parameter-free, computationally affordable ensemble; applied to models from papers at recent machine learning and computer vision venues.

papers.title: Dos and Don'ts of Machine Learning in Computer Security
papers.key_idea: Identifies common pitfalls in the design, implementation and evaluation of learning-based security systems, finds them widespread in 30 top-conference security papers, and gives actionable recommendations to avoid or mitigate them.
papers.method: Pitfall catalogue; prevalence study over 30 papers from top-tier security conferences of the past 10 years; empirical analysis of how individual pitfalls lead to unrealistic performance.

papers.title: Motivating the Rules of the Game for Adversarial Example Research
papers.key_idea: Argues that defense papers study abstract games unrelated to concrete security concerns; gives a taxonomy of attacker motivations, constraints and abilities and recommendations for clearer threat models and more meaningful evaluation.
papers.method: Position paper with a taxonomy of plausible adversaries and a list of recommendations.

papers.title: Adversarial Risk and the Dangers of Evaluating Against Weak Attacks
papers.key_idea: Treats common attacks as tractable surrogates of true adversarial risk: a defense may only be obscure to the attack used. Gradient-free optimization attacks drive several defenses to near-zero accuracy.
papers.method: Formalizes obscurity to an adversary; tools and heuristics to identify obscured models; gradient-free optimization techniques repurposed as attacks.

papers.title: Indicators of Attack Failure: Debugging and Improving Optimization of Adversarial Examples
papers.key_idea: Categorizes how the optimization of gradient-based attacks fails, proposes six indicators that detect such failures automatically and a protocol of fixes, turning evaluation guidelines into systematic debugging tests.
papers.method: Failure taxonomy for gradient-based attack optimization; six automatic indicators; systematic protocol to apply the corresponding fixes.

papers.title: Evaluating the Adversarial Robustness of Adaptive Test-time Defenses
papers.key_idea: Categorizes defenses that optimize at test time and re-evaluates a representative set: none clearly improves on static defenses, some weaken the model and add inference cost; extends the Carlini checklist with steps for such defenses.
papers.method: Taxonomy of adaptive test-time defenses; careful case-study evaluation of recent defenses for image classification; recommendations and concrete checklist steps.

papers.title: "Real Attackers Don't Compute Gradients": Bridging the Gap Between Adversarial ML Research and Practice
papers.venue: 2023 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML)
papers.key_idea: Position paper: real attackers use simple tactics, so research threat models miss practice; three real-world case studies, a review of adversarial ML papers at top security venues, and calls for precise, cost-driven threat modelling.
papers.method: Three real-world case studies; analysis of all adversarial ML papers recently published at top security conferences; position statements.

papers.title: Adversarial Examples Are Not Easily Detected: Bypassing Ten Detection Methods
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 10th ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security
papers.key_idea: Surveys ten proposed detectors of adversarial examples and defeats all of them with newly constructed loss functions; properties believed intrinsic to adversarial examples are not, and simple guidelines for evaluating future defenses are proposed.
papers.method: For each of ten detection proposals an attacker-side loss function is constructed that takes the detector into account; the detectors are compared in efficacy.

papers.title: Adversarial Example Defenses: Ensembles of Weak Defenses are not Strong
papers.key_idea: Asks whether combining several weak defenses yields a strong one: for three ensemble defenses and all their components an adaptive adversary finds low-distortion adversarial examples, so ensembles of weak defenses are not sufficient.
papers.method: Adaptive attacks against two recently proposed defenses that combine components by design and against a third defense that combines three independent defenses.

papers.title: Evading Adversarial Example Detection Defenses with Orthogonal Projected Gradient Descent
papers.key_idea: Evading a detector requires inputs that are misclassified and also judged non-adversarial; orthogonalizing the two gradients stops attacks from over-optimizing one constraint at the cost of the other.
papers.method: Orthogonal Projected Gradient Descent: gradient orthogonalization inside standard gradient-based attacks.

papers.title: Detecting Adversarial Examples Is (Nearly) As Hard As Classifying Them
papers.key_idea: Proves a reduction: a robust detector for attacks at distance epsilon yields an inefficient but similarly robust classifier at distance epsilon/2, which gives a sanity check on whether claimed detection results are plausible.
papers.method: Theoretical hardness reduction between detection and classification of adversarial examples; applied as a sanity check to published detector defenses.

papers.title: Are Odds Really Odd? Bypassing Statistical Detection of Adversarial Examples
papers.key_idea: A logit-mimicry attack makes adversarial logits resemble benign ones and defeats a statistical-test detector reported at 99% TPR and 1% FPR; a detector retrained on such examples is evaded again by an adaptive attacker.
papers.method: Classifier-based adaptation of the statistical test; Logit Mimicry Attack; adaptive attack on a detector trained with mimicry examples; iterative retraining.

papers.title: Interpretable Deep Learning under Fire
papers.key_idea: ADV^2 attacks craft inputs that mislead a classifier and its coupled interpretation model at once, so the attacker can choose both the prediction and the explanation shown for an adversarial input.
papers.method: Joint optimization against the model and its interpreter; evaluated against four major types of interpretable deep learning systems; analysis of the prediction-interpretation gap; countermeasures explored.

papers.title: Zero-Query Transfer Attacks on Context-Aware Object Detectors
papers.venue: 2022 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: Builds context-consistent attack plans that give victim objects wrong labels without breaking scene context, so the attack evades the context-consistency check of a black-box detector without any query to the victim.
papers.method: Derives several context-consistent attack plans, filters them with a perturbation success probability matrix and implements the chosen plan with a perturbation-bounded attack; compared with a few-query scheme and with context-agnostic attacks.

papers.title: The base-rate fallacy and the difficulty of intrusion detection
papers.venue: ACM Transactions on Information and System Security
papers.key_idea: Under reasonable assumptions the false alarm rate, not the detection rate, limits an intrusion detector: a useful probability that an alarm is a real intrusion requires a very low false alarm rate (base-rate fallacy).
papers.method: Bayesian analysis of the probability of an intrusion given an alarm; review of a selection of reported intrusion detection results.

papers.title: Membership Inference Attacks From First Principles
papers.venue: 2022 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (SP)
papers.key_idea: Argues that average-case accuracy metrics cannot show whether an attack is confident about any sample; evaluation should report the true-positive rate at low false-positive rates, for example below 0.1%.
papers.method: Metric argument, then a likelihood ratio attack for membership inference that combines several ideas from the literature.

papers.title: Quickest Change Detection
papers.venue: Academic Press Library in Signal Processing
papers.key_idea: Tutorial on quickest change detection: detect a change in the distribution of a monitored stream as quickly as possible subject to false-alarm constraints, in Bayesian and minimax formulations with optimal or asymptotically optimal procedures.
papers.method: Tutorial chapter: problem formulations, optimal and asymptotically optimal solutions, generalizations and extensions, applications and open issues.

papers.title: Towards a Rigorous Evaluation of Time-series Anomaly Detection
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.key_idea: Shows that the point-adjustment protocol used before scoring time-series anomaly detectors inflates F1 so much that random scores look state of the art; proposes a new baseline and evaluation protocol.
papers.method: Theoretical and experimental analysis of the point-adjustment protocol; comparison with a random anomaly score and with an untrained model.

papers.title: Limiting the Impact of Stealthy Attacks on Industrial Control Systems
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 2016 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security
papers.key_idea: Title-level only: attack detection for industrial control systems judged by how far it limits attackers who stay stealthy. Memory lead, UNVERIFIED: a metric relating stealthy-attack impact to a bound on false alarms.

papers.title: Confidence-Calibrated Adversarial Training: Generalizing to Unseen Attacks
papers.key_idea: Confidence-calibrated adversarial training makes adversarial examples low-confidence so they can be rejected; it is evaluated with attacks that maximise confidence and with worst-case, confidence-thresholded robust test error across attacks.
papers.method: Training that biases the model towards low confidence on adversarial examples, with rejection by a confidence threshold; new white-box and black-box attacks that directly maximise confidence.

papers.title: Stealthy Attacks against Robotic Vehicles Protected by Control-based Intrusion Detection Techniques
papers.key_idea: Three kinds of stealthy attacks evade control-based intrusion detection on robotic vehicles and still disrupt missions; automated algorithms run them without detailed knowledge of the vehicle.
papers.method: Analysis of weaknesses in control-based intrusion detection; three stealthy attack types with automated algorithms; tests against an intrusion detection system that monitors the runtime behaviour of the vehicle.

papers.title: Exploring the Physical-World Adversarial Robustness of Vehicle Detection
papers.key_idea: A CARLA-based instant-level generation pipeline builds the DCI dataset, used to compare three vehicle detectors under three physical adversarial attacks across discrete and continuous scene changes, weather included.
papers.method: CARLA simulator renders attacked vehicles at discrete and continuous instants; detectors are scored by average precision per attack, scene type and weather.

papers.title: Connecting the Digital and Physical World: Improving the Robustness of Adversarial Attacks
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.key_idea: Learns the digital-to-physical change with an image-to-image translation network and optimises adversarial examples through it, so they keep working after printing and photographing.
papers.method: Image-to-image translation network trained to imitate the digital-to-physical process, placed inside the attack optimisation.

papers.title: Reconstruction-Based Adversarial Attack Detection in Vision-Based Autonomous Driving Systems
papers.key_idea: A deep-autoencoder detector for attacks on the regression models of a driving system, judged with offline metrics and with an online framework that checks robustness end to end at runtime.
papers.method: Natural-noise perturbations and adapted square, HopSkipJump and boundary attacks on regression models; the autoencoder reconstruction loss flags attacked inputs.

papers.title: WIP: Adversarial Object-Evasion Attack Detection in Autonomous Driving Contexts: A Simulation-Based Investigation Using YOLO
papers.venue: Proceedings Symposium on Vehicle Security & Privacy
papers.key_idea: Title-level reading: work-in-progress study of detecting object-evasion attacks against a YOLO detector inside simulated driving contexts.
papers.method: Not read beyond the title.

papers.title: PASS: A System-Driven Evaluation Platform for Autonomous Driving Safety and Security
papers.venue: Proceedings Fourth International Workshop on Automotive and Autonomous Vehicle Security
papers.key_idea: Title-level reading: a system-driven evaluation platform for the safety and security of autonomous driving.
papers.method: Not read beyond the title. Row P2-P1022 (LIT_X1, SoK abstract) describes PASS as an open-source, simulation-centric platform; not read by this agent.

papers.title: SlowTrack: Increasing the Latency of Camera-Based Perception in Autonomous Driving Using Adversarial Examples
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.key_idea: Adversarial examples that raise the execution time of the whole camera-based perception pipeline, not only the detector, judged by vehicle crash rate in a full-stack simulation.
papers.method: Two-stage attack with three new loss functions; tested on four camera-based perception pipelines and, for system-level effects, on Baidu Apollo with the LGSVL simulator in two scenarios.

papers.title: Security of Deep Learning based Lane Keeping System under Physical-World Adversarial Attack
papers.key_idea: Dirty road patches as a physical threat model against DNN lane-keeping assistance, optimised over consecutive camera frames whose attacks depend on each other.
papers.method: Optimisation formulation of the road patch that handles the dependencies among attacks on consecutive frames; evaluated on one state-of-the-art LKAS.

papers.title: Attacking vision-based perception in end-to-end autonomous driving models
papers.key_idea: Physically realizable attacks on end-to-end driving models in simulation: road lines painted by Bayesian-optimised design make the car fail, for example in right turns, or follow a path chosen by the attacker.
papers.method: Objective functions for attack success at the driving level; Bayesian optimisation over line parameters; network deconvolution to inspect why attacks work.

papers.title: DeepBillboard
papers.venue: Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 42nd International Conference on Software Engineering
papers.key_idea: Printable adversarial billboards beside the road that push the steering angle of DNN driving models off course across changing view angle, distance and lighting, tested digitally and physically.
papers.method: Optimisation that maximises the chance, size and duration of steering-angle errors during a drive past the billboard; digital and physical-world experiments.

papers.title: CARLA: An Open Urban Driving Simulator
papers.key_idea: Open-source urban driving simulator with open digital assets, configurable sensor suites and environmental conditions, introduced with a comparison of modular, imitation-learning and reinforcement-learning driving approaches.
papers.method: Simulator platform; three driving approaches evaluated in controlled scenarios of increasing difficulty with the simulator's own metrics.

papers.title: LGSVL Simulator: A High Fidelity Simulator for Autonomous Driving
papers.key_idea: High-fidelity simulator for end-to-end, full-stack testing that connects to the open Autoware and Apollo driving stacks, with tools to customise sensors, add controllable objects and build digital twins.
papers.method: Simulator engine plus tools; description paper.

papers.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Semantic Segmentation for Autonomous Driving against Real-World Adversarial Patch Attacks
papers.venue: 2022 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
papers.key_idea: Runs one patch-attack family through digital, simulator and physical stages against semantic segmentation: EOT on Cityscapes, a CARLA scene-specific attack, then a printed billboard on a real road.
papers.method: EOT extended to segmentation on Cityscapes; scene-specific optimisation in the CARLA simulator for transfer to 3D scenes; outdoor test with a printed billboard patch.

papers.title: Universal Physical Camouflage Attacks on Object Detectors
papers.key_idea: Learns one camouflage pattern per object category that fools detector proposals, classification and regression, and introduces AttackScenes, a controllable virtual 3D database for comparing physical attacks reproducibly.
papers.method: Joint attack on region proposal network, classifier and regressor; transformations that mimic deformable surfaces; naturalness constraint; evaluation in AttackScenes and in real environments.

papers.title: Adversarial examples in the physical world
papers.key_idea: Adversarial images seen through a cell-phone camera still mislead an ImageNet Inception classifier in a large fraction of cases, so camera-fed systems are exposed, not only direct-input ones.
papers.method: Adversarial images captured with a cell-phone camera and fed to an ImageNet Inception classifier; classification accuracy measured.

papers.title: Synthesizing Robust Adversarial Examples
papers.key_idea: Optimises adversarial examples over a chosen distribution of transformations (noise, distortion, affine change, viewpoint) so they survive physical capture; used to 3D-print adversarial objects.
papers.method: Optimisation over a distribution of transformations; 2D images robust to noise, distortion and affine change; 3D objects manufactured by 3D printing.

papers.title: NO Need to Worry about Adversarial Examples in Object Detection in Autonomous Vehicles
papers.key_idea: Experiments suggesting that printed physical adversarial images do not disrupt recognition from a moving platform: photos taken at varied distances and angles are mostly classified correctly.
papers.method: Perturbed images printed and photographed from different distances and angles; the photos are classified by the trained network.

papers.title: Standard detectors aren't (currently) fooled by physical adversarial stop signs
papers.key_idea: Argues that published physical adversarial stop signs fool a crop-and-classify proxy but not standard YOLO and Faster R-CNN detectors, because detectors search for their own boxes across scale and view.
papers.method: Earlier physical adversarial stop signs tested against YOLO and Faster RCNN in standard configuration; analysis of the cropping and resizing in the proxy setup.

papers.title: PhysGAN: Generating Physical-World-Resilient Adversarial Examples for Autonomous Driving
papers.venue: 2020 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
papers.key_idea: A generative model that produces physically placeable adversarial examples, not whole-scene pixel noise, that keep misleading steering models continuously during a drive; tested digitally and in the real world.
papers.method: GAN-based generation of physical-world-resilient examples; comparison with state-of-the-art and self-designed baselines; digital and real-world evaluations.
